## Breaking changes

### General

#### Nelm and werf binaries are built with Go 1.26 and require macOS 12 or later

<a id="distribution-os-requirements-go-1-26"></a>`distribution-os-requirements-go-1-26` · change · `distribution` `platform` · products: nelm, werf

Before: werf v2 release binaries were built with Go 1.23, which supports macOS 11 Big Sur and Linux kernel 2.6.32 or later. Nelm v1 release binaries were built with Go 1.24, which supports macOS 11 Big Sur and Linux kernel 3.2 or later.
Now: werf v3 and Nelm v2 are built with Go 1.26 (the `go` directive of their modules is `1.26`), so the macOS binaries require macOS 12 Monterey or later and the Linux binaries require kernel 3.2 or later (for Nelm the Linux requirement is unchanged). The set of published platforms is unchanged (`linux-amd64`, `linux-arm64`, `darwin-amd64`, `darwin-arm64`, `windows-amd64`).

**Migration:** Upgrade macOS hosts older than 12 Monterey before installing werf v3 or Nelm v2. werf only: upgrade Linux hosts with a kernel older than 3.2 before installing werf v3.

**References:** [werf@bc51d7214](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/bc51d7214f8e), [werf@dec66c577](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/dec66c577729), [nelm@d08c2937f](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/d08c2937f962), [nelm@fc44780e6](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/fc44780e6b4c), <https://go.dev/doc/go1.25#darwin>, <https://go.dev/doc/go1.24#linux>

#### The `preview-v2` feature gate is removed, its features are always on

<a id="feature-gate-preview-v2-removed"></a>`feature-gate-preview-v2-removed` · removal · `cli` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `NELM_FEAT_PREVIEW_V2=true` enabled at once the features planned for Nelm v2: `remote-charts`, `field-sensitive`, `clean-null-fields`, `more-detailed-exit-code-for-plan`, `native-release-list`, `native-release-uninstall` (and others). Each could also be enabled with its own `NELM_FEAT_*` variable.
Now: these behaviors are the default and their feature gates, including `preview-v2`, are removed. Setting a removed `NELM_FEAT_*` variable only prints an `Unsupported environment variable(s)` warning.

**Migration:** Remove `NELM_FEAT_PREVIEW_V2`, `NELM_FEAT_REMOTE_CHARTS`, `NELM_FEAT_FIELD_SENSITIVE`, `NELM_FEAT_CLEAN_NULL_FIELDS`, `NELM_FEAT_MORE_DETAILED_EXIT_CODE_FOR_PLAN`, `NELM_FEAT_RESOURCE_VALIDATION`, `NELM_FEAT_NATIVE_RELEASE_LIST` and `NELM_FEAT_NATIVE_RELEASE_UNINSTALL` from the environment. If you did not use `preview-v2`, review the entries for each of these features: their behavior is now always on.

**References:** [nelm@07f2dfccd](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/07f2dfccdde2), [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc)

#### The werf Go module path is `github.com/werf/werf/v3`

<a id="werf-go-module-path-v3"></a>`werf-go-module-path-v3` · change · `distribution` · products: werf

Before: werf v2 was the Go module `github.com/werf/werf/v2` (e.g. `go install github.com/werf/werf/v2/cmd/werf@...`, imports `github.com/werf/werf/v2/pkg/...`).
Now: werf v3 is the Go module `github.com/werf/werf/v3`. The CLI, its flags and configuration formats are not affected; only building werf from source or importing its packages is.

**Migration:** Build or install werf v3 from `github.com/werf/werf/v3/cmd/werf`, and replace `github.com/werf/werf/v2/` with `github.com/werf/werf/v3/` in Go imports.

**References:** [werf#7909](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7909)

#### The werf binary no longer acts as Helm when invoked as `helm` or with `WERF_HELM3_MODE=1`

<a id="cli-helm-compatibility-mode-removed"></a>`cli-helm-compatibility-mode-removed` · removal · `cli` · products: werf

Before: when the werf binary was invoked under the name `helm` (for example through a symlink `helm -> werf`) or with `WERF_HELM3_MODE=1`, it ran the `werf helm` command tree as the root command, so `helm install ...` worked as `werf helm install ...`.
Now: the binary always starts as `werf`; the file name and `WERF_HELM3_MODE` are ignored.

**Migration:** Remove `helm -> werf` symlinks and `WERF_HELM3_MODE`. Use the upstream Helm CLI or Nelm where a `helm` binary is expected, and call `werf helm <subcommand>` explicitly for the subcommands werf still provides.

**References:** [werf@301c8f90d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/301c8f90d859)

#### Unknown keys in `werf-giterminism.yaml` are a validation error

<a id="giterminism-strict-schema-validation"></a>`giterminism-strict-schema-validation` · change · `giterminism` `validation` · products: werf

Before: the `werf-giterminism.yaml` schema accepted any additional properties, so unknown or misspelled keys (for example, `config.allowUncommited`) were silently ignored.
Now: every object in the schema rejects unknown keys, and werf fails with an error naming the offending key, such as `config.allowUncommited in body is a forbidden property`. The valid `config.secrets` (`allowEnvVariables`, `allowFiles`, `allowValueIds`) and `includes.allowIncludesUpdate` keys are now part of the schema and are type-checked.

**Migration:** Fix or remove unknown and misspelled keys in `werf-giterminism.yaml`.

**References:** [werf#7604](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7604), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#validation-of-werf-giterminismyaml>

#### `--docker-compose-bin-path` is removed from `werf compose` commands

<a id="compose-docker-compose-bin-path-removed"></a>`compose-docker-compose-bin-path-removed` · removal · `compose` `cli` · products: werf

Before: `werf compose` commands accepted `--docker-compose-bin-path` (`$WERF_DOCKER_COMPOSE_BIN_PATH`), deprecated and ignored because `docker compose` is always used.
Now: the flag is removed; passing it is an argument parsing error. `$WERF_DOCKER_COMPOSE_BIN_PATH` is ignored.

**Migration:** Remove `--docker-compose-bin-path` from `werf compose` invocations.

**References:** [werf#7629](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7629)

#### `werf ci-env github` no longer logs in to `docker.pkg.github.com`

<a id="ci-env-github-legacy-registry-login-removed"></a>`ci-env-github-legacy-registry-login-removed` · removal · `ci-env` `registry` · products: werf

Before: in GitHub Actions, when `WERF_REPO` started with `docker.pkg.github.com`, `werf ci-env github` logged in to that legacy GitHub Packages registry instead of `ghcr.io`.
Now: `werf ci-env github` always logs in to `ghcr.io`.

**Migration:** Move images from `docker.pkg.github.com` to `ghcr.io` (GitHub has retired the old registry), or log in to the legacy registry yourself with `docker login`.

**References:** [werf#7629](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7629)

#### `werf ci-env` uses `DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG` automatically when it is set

<a id="ci-env-docker-auth-config-auto"></a>`ci-env-docker-auth-config-auto` · change · `ci-env` `registry` · products: werf

Before: `werf ci-env` generated the session Docker config from `DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG` only with `--use-docker-auth-config` (`$WERF_USE_DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG=true`); otherwise it copied the current Docker config (`~/.docker/config.json` or `$DOCKER_CONFIG`).
Now: if `DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG` is non-empty and neither `--use-docker-auth-config` nor `WERF_USE_DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG` is set, `werf ci-env` generates the Docker config from `DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG`. The generated config replaces the current one rather than being merged with it, so credentials and credential helpers from the existing Docker config are no longer used. An explicit flag or environment variable, including `false`, still takes precedence.

**Migration:** If your CI sets `DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG` but relies on credentials from the existing Docker config, pass `--use-docker-auth-config=false` or set `WERF_USE_DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG=false`, or add those credentials to `DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG`.

**References:** [werf#7624](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7624), [werf#7692](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7692), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#registry-credentials>

#### `werf kubectl` is upgraded from kubectl 1.29 to kubectl 1.37

<a id="kubectl-embedded-version-1-37"></a>`kubectl-embedded-version-1-37` · change · `kubectl` `dependencies` · products: werf

Before: `werf kubectl` embedded kubectl v1.29 (`k8s.io/kubectl` v0.29.3), and werf used the Kubernetes v0.29 client libraries.
Now: `werf kubectl` embeds kubectl v1.37 (`k8s.io/kubectl` v0.37.0) with the Kubernetes v0.37 client libraries. Commands, flags and output follow kubectl 1.37. Changes visible in the werf CLI reference:
- Changed: `werf kubectl autoscale` replaces `--cpu-percent` with `--cpu` and adds `--memory`; `werf kubectl debug --profile` defaults to `general` instead of `legacy` (the `legacy` profile is gone; `sysadmin` is added); `werf kubectl wait --for` can be repeated; `werf kubectl config set-context` accepts `-n` for `--namespace`; `werf kubectl explain` accepts `-o` and `-R`.
- kuberc: kubectl preferences (default flag values and aliases) are read from a kuberc file (`~/.kube/kuberc` by default, or `--kuberc`), which can be disabled with `KUBECTL_KUBERC=false`. New commands `werf kubectl kuberc view` and `werf kubectl kuberc set` (`--section`, `--command`, `--option`, `--name`, `--prependarg`, `--appendarg`, `--overwrite`, `--policy`, `--allowlist-entry`) manage it.
- New flags of all `werf kubectl` commands: `--as-user-extra`, `--kuberc`, `--proxy-url`.
- New command flags: `api-resources --show-managed-fields`; `apply --subresource`; `attach --detach-keys`; `config set-credentials --exec-interactive-mode`, `--exec-provide-cluster-info`; `debug --custom`, `--keep-annotations`, `--keep-init-containers`, `--keep-labels`, `--keep-liveness`, `--keep-readiness`, `--keep-startup`; `diff --show-secrets`; `explain --max-depth`; `kustomize --helm-debug`; `logs --all-pods`; `run --cascade`, `--detach-keys`, `--force`, `--grace-period`, `--kustomize`, `--recursive`, `--timeout`, `--wait`; `top node` and `top pod --show-swap`.

**Migration:** Check scripts that call `werf kubectl` against the kubectl changelog between v1.29 and v1.37 and adjust removed or changed flags: replace `autoscale --cpu-percent=N` with `--cpu=N%`, and pass `--profile=general` (or another existing profile) to `debug` instead of `legacy`. If a kuberc file on the host must not affect `werf kubectl`, set `KUBECTL_KUBERC=false`.

**References:** [werf@301c8f90d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/301c8f90d859), [werf@bc51d7214](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/bc51d7214f8e), [werf#7499](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7499), [werf@fcf48b426](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/fcf48b426014)

#### werf detects colored output itself: ci-env no longer exports `WERF_LOG_COLOR_MODE`, and render commands honor `--log-color-mode`

<a id="logging-color-mode-auto-detected"></a>`logging-color-mode-auto-detected` · change · `logging` `ci-env` · products: werf

Before: `werf ci-env gitlab` and `werf ci-env github` exported `WERF_LOG_COLOR_MODE=on` (`off` for GitLab 12.1.4–12.1.x) to force colors in CI, and `werf render` and `werf bundle render` always printed manifests without colors, ignoring `--log-color-mode`.
Now: `werf ci-env` no longer exports `WERF_LOG_COLOR_MODE`; with the default `--log-color-mode=auto` werf uses the Nelm color detection, which enables colors in GitLab CI and GitHub Actions and disables them for machine-readable output. `werf render` and `werf bundle render` honor `--log-color-mode`: `on` colors the rendered manifests, `auto` keeps them uncolored in CI.

**Migration:** No action needed in most cases. Set `WERF_LOG_COLOR_MODE=on` or `off` explicitly if your CI relied on the value exported by `werf ci-env`.
If the output of `werf render` or `werf bundle render` goes to a file, `kubectl` or a YAML parser, make sure the color mode is not forced to `on` there: remove an inherited `WERF_LOG_COLOR_MODE=on` or `--log-color-mode=on`, or pass `--log-color-mode=off`, otherwise the manifests contain ANSI color codes.

**References:** [werf#7536](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7536)

### Build

#### A trailing slash in `to:` of `git` and `import` is a configuration error

<a id="build-trailing-slash-in-to-error"></a>`build-trailing-slash-in-to-error` · change · `stapel` `config` `validation` · products: werf

Before: a `to:` path with a trailing slash (for example, `to: /usr/sbin/`) in a Stapel `git` mapping or `import` only printed a warning, and werf treated it as `to: /usr/sbin`, copying the source itself to that path rather than into the directory.
Now: such a path is a configuration error. `to: /` is still allowed.

**Migration:** Remove the trailing slash, checking the intended destination: if `add` is a directory, its contents are merged into `to`; if `add` is a file, it is copied into `to` when `to` is an existing directory, otherwise `to` is the file's path. To avoid ambiguity, specify the full destination file name.

**References:** [werf#7627](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7627), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#file-imports>

#### Build-time variables `COLUMNS`, `WERF_COMMIT_*` and `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` no longer end up in the image `ENV`

<a id="build-time-env-not-in-image-config"></a>`build-time-env-not-in-image-config` · fix · `stapel` `images` · products: werf

Before: Stapel images built with the Docker server or Buildah backend got `COLUMNS`, `WERF_COMMIT_HASH`, `WERF_COMMIT_TIME_HUMAN`, `WERF_COMMIT_TIME_UNIX` and `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` baked into the `ENV` of the image config, although these variables are meant only for build commands. When `imageSpec` was configured, werf additionally removed the `WERF_COMMIT_*` variables from the final image, including ones inherited from the base image.
Now: these variables are available to build commands only and are not stored in the image config. The implicit removal of `WERF_COMMIT_*` by `imageSpec` is gone, so such variables inherited from a base image built by an older werf stay in the image.

**Migration:** If your images are based on images built by werf v2 that contain `WERF_COMMIT_*` variables and you do not want them, list them in `imageSpec.config.removeEnv`. Do not rely on `COLUMNS`, `WERF_COMMIT_*` or `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` being present in the built image at runtime.

**References:** [werf#7620](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7620), [werf#7651](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7651)

#### Built images no longer carry the `werf.io/base-image-id` label

<a id="build-base-image-id-label-removed"></a>`build-base-image-id-label-removed` · removal · `images` `cleanup` · products: werf

Before: werf labeled every built stage with `werf.io/base-image-id` (the ID of the image it was built on), and `werf cleanup` used this label as an extra fallback to protect ancestors of kept stages.
Now: the label is no longer set or read. Ancestor tracking and cleanup protection rely on the `werf.io/parent-stage-id` label only.

**Migration:** If your tooling reads `werf.io/base-image-id` from images, switch to `werf.io/parent-stage-id`.

**References:** [werf#7631](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7631)

#### Dockerfile builds on the Docker backend always use BuildKit; `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0` no longer selects the legacy builder

<a id="build-docker-legacy-builder-removed"></a>`build-docker-legacy-builder-removed` · removal · `dockerfile` · products: werf

Before: with the Docker server backend, Dockerfile images were built with BuildKit (buildx) by default, but `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0` or `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=false` switched werf to the legacy Docker builder.
Now: werf builds Dockerfiles through the upstream buildx API only. The legacy builder is gone and `DOCKER_BUILDKIT` is ignored.

**Migration:** Remove `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0`/`false` from the environment and check that your Dockerfiles build with BuildKit.

**References:** [werf@efe60d89d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/efe60d89dc3e), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#builders-and-image-configuration>

#### Git LFS file contents are included automatically in Stapel git mappings and Dockerfile contexts

<a id="build-git-lfs-content"></a>`build-git-lfs-content` · feature · `git` `stapel` `dockerfile` · products: werf

Before: files exported from Git into images followed the host's checkout filters, so the same commit could produce LFS contents on one host and LFS pointer files on another.
Now: LFS pointers in the selected commit are recognized by their contents (regardless of `.gitattributes`) and the real objects are downloaded and verified (size and SHA-256) for files selected by git mapping paths or Dockerfile context filtering; no `lfs` directive or `git lfs install` is needed. `git-lfs` must be discoverable by Git when selected files contain LFS pointers, and missing objects fail the build. Git credentials, `url.*.insteadOf` and the commit's `.lfsconfig` are honored. LFS files inside submodules and pointer extensions are rejected. Git archive caches, Git-stage digests and non-staged Dockerfile digests change once, so affected images are rebuilt.

**Migration:** Install `git-lfs` where werf runs if your repositories contain LFS files used in images, and make sure LFS objects are downloadable. Expect a one-time rebuild of images built from Git.

**References:** [werf#8042](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8042)

#### Image names in werf.yaml are validated when the configuration is loaded

<a id="build-image-name-validation"></a>`build-image-name-validation` · change · `config` `validation` · products: werf

Before: any image name was accepted at config loading; a name that a Go template rendered empty or malformed (for example `/api` or `<no value>`) failed only later in the build phase with an `invalid reference format` error.
Now: names are checked when the configuration is loaded and an invalid name is a configuration error pointing at the offending line. Latin letters, digits, `_`, `.`, `-` and `+` are allowed, with optional `/`-separated segments; each segment must start with a letter or digit. For example `modules/controller` and `libstdc++` are valid, while an empty name, whitespace, `/api` and `modules//controller` are not. In `werf compose` and env-file build reports, `+` in an image name is replaced with `_` in environment variable names (`libstdc++` uses the `WERF_LIBSTDC___` prefix).

**Migration:** Rename images whose names do not match the rules, including names produced by Go templates.

**References:** [werf#7711](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7711), [werf#7848](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7848), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#image-names>

#### Nameless images (`image: ~`) are no longer supported

<a id="config-nameless-image-removed"></a>`config-nameless-image-removed` · removal · `config` `images` · products: werf

Before: `werf.yaml` could contain a single image without a name (`image: ~`, deprecated with a warning); its name in commands and templates was empty, and the service values contained `.Values.werf.is_nameless_image` and `.Values.werf.nameless_image`.
Now: `image: ~` fails with `nameless image (image: ~) is not supported, please specify an image name!`, and `is_nameless_image`/`nameless_image` are no longer in the service values.

**Migration:** Give the image a name (e.g. `image: app`), and use `.Values.werf.image.app` (or the corresponding name in commands such as `werf run app`) instead of `.Values.werf.nameless_image`.

**References:** [werf@7e23a855d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/7e23a855d1b0), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#image-names>

#### Omitted `git.stageDependencies` default to `**/*`, so changes of Git files rerun Shell stages

<a id="build-stage-dependencies-default"></a>`build-stage-dependencies-default` · change · `stapel` `git` `cache` · products: werf

Before: when `git.stageDependencies` was absent (or `{}`) for a git mapping, changes of the mapped files alone never reran `install`, `beforeSetup` or `setup`; every omitted stage had no Git-file dependency.
Now: an absent or empty `stageDependencies` block gives all three stages `**/*`: any change of a file added by the git mapping (respecting `includePaths`/`excludePaths`) reruns the first configured Shell stage and the following ones, like `COPY` before `RUN` in a Dockerfile. In a partially filled block, omitted stages before the last explicitly declared stage (in the order `install` → `beforeSetup` → `setup`) get `[]`, and those after it get `**/*`. An explicit `[]` still means no Git-file dependency.

**Migration:** Expect additional rebuilds. To keep a stage free of direct Git-file dependencies, set it to `[]` explicitly; to depend only on some files, list their masks.

**References:** [werf#7531](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7531), [werf@5a83a7a1c](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/5a83a7a1cf9e), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#git-dependencies-of-build-stages>

#### One `from` key refers to both werf.yaml images and external images; `fromImage`, `import.image` and `dependencies.image` are deprecated

<a id="build-unified-from-directive"></a>`build-unified-from-directive` · change · `config` `stapel` `images` · products: werf

Before: a Stapel base image was set with `from:` (always an external image) or `fromImage:` (an image from `werf.yaml`); file imports used `import.image` (with `import.from` as an alias), and image dependencies used `dependencies.image` (werf v2 also accepted `dependencies.from`, which silently won over `dependencies.image` when both were set). A base `from: ubuntu` without a tag was pulled as `ubuntu:latest`.
Now: `from` is the single key in all three places — `from:` for the Stapel base image, `import.from` and `dependencies.from`. A name defined in `werf.yaml` refers to that internal image; anything else is an external image reference. An external reference in a Stapel base `from` or in `import.from` must include a tag or digest (`from: ubuntu` is a configuration error; use `ubuntu:latest`, `ubuntu:TAG` or `ubuntu@sha256:...`). `from: scratch` needs no tag; `scratch` is now a reserved image name, and `from: scratch` is rejected in `import.from` and together with `fromLatest`.
`fromImage`, `import.image` and `dependencies.image` still work but print a deprecation warning. Specifying an old key together with its `from` replacement is a configuration error.

**Migration:** Add a tag or digest to every external image reference in a Stapel base `from` and in `import.from` (for example, `from: ubuntu` → `from: ubuntu:latest`). Rename an image called `scratch`, if any.
Optionally rename `fromImage` → `from`, `import.image` → `import.from` and `dependencies.image` → `dependencies.from`; use only one of the old and new keys in the same place.

**References:** [werf@b11ca78b4](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/b11ca78b4cb1), [werf@0679f0237](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/0679f0237d1d), [werf#7628](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7628), [werf#7639](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7639), [werf#7692](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7692), [werf@9f52c5cee](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/9f52c5cee7f7), [werf@d57b2fccd](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/d57b2fccd34c), [werf#7944](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7944), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#one-from-key-for-image-references>

#### Several Stapel imports can target the same directory, without automatic excludes between them

<a id="build-multiple-imports-same-target"></a>`build-multiple-imports-same-target` · change · `stapel` `config` · products: werf

Before: two `import` entries of an image whose `to` paths were equal or nested failed configuration validation with `Conflict between imports!` unless werf could separate them with automatic excludes; when the imports had `includePaths`, werf silently added the included paths of one import to the `excludePaths` of the other.
Now: imports are no longer checked against each other, and werf no longer adds automatic excludes between them: several imports may copy into the same or nested target directories, applied one after another. Existing configurations that relied on automatic excludes now copy the previously excluded files too, so a later import can overwrite files of an earlier one. Conflicts between `git` mappings and between `git` mappings and imports are still checked.

**Migration:** Review `import` entries of each image whose `to` paths are equal or nested. To keep the previous separation, add the paths werf used to exclude automatically to `excludePaths` explicitly; otherwise order the imports deliberately and verify the resulting files in the image.

**References:** [werf#7537](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7537)

#### Staged Dockerfile builds always use the v2 implementation; `WERF_STAGED_DOCKERFILE_VERSION` is removed

<a id="build-staged-dockerfile-v2-only"></a>`build-staged-dockerfile-v2-only` · removal · `dockerfile` · products: werf

Before: Dockerfile images with `staged: true` used the `v1` builder by default; `WERF_STAGED_DOCKERFILE_VERSION=v2` enabled a dedicated `FROM` layer for caching the base image, with dependencies expanded after `FROM` and the base image environment propagated.
Now: the `v2` implementation is always used, and `WERF_STAGED_DOCKERFILE_VERSION` is ignored (`v1` can no longer be selected).

**Migration:** Remove `WERF_STAGED_DOCKERFILE_VERSION` from the environment and check staged Dockerfile builds with the `v2` behavior.

**References:** [werf#7644](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7644), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#builders-and-image-configuration>

#### Stages built by werf v2 are not reused: the first v3 build rebuilds all images

<a id="build-v2-stage-cache-not-reused"></a>`build-v2-stage-cache-not-reused` · change · `cache` · products: werf

Before: stage digests stayed compatible across werf v2 releases, so new versions reused stages already present in `--repo`.
Now: the build cache version is bumped (`1.2` → `2.0`) and digest calculation changed in several places (current stage names such as `dependenciesBeforeInstall` instead of legacy `importsBeforeInstall`, `linux/amd64` included in digests like other platforms, the base image reference always included in the `FROM` stage of staged Dockerfiles, new content-based tags). No stage built by v2 matches, so the first v3 build rebuilds every image and pushes new stages next to the v2 ones.

**Migration:** Plan time and registry space for a full rebuild when switching to v3. If v2 and v3 share `--repo`, protect the v2 images you need for rollback from `werf cleanup` (for example, with `--keep-list`).

**References:** [werf@55dc5ea4b](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/55dc5ea4b013), [werf#7629](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7629), [werf#7644](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7644), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#building>

#### Stapel applies Git changes on the Docker backend by copying files instead of `git apply`

<a id="build-stapel-git-patches-via-archive"></a>`build-stapel-git-patches-via-archive` · change · `stapel` `git` · products: werf

Before: with the Docker server backend, Stapel applied text changes of Git files in the `gitCache`/`gitLatestPatch` and `stageDependencies` stages with `git apply`; if a `git`-mapped file had been modified by an earlier `install`/`beforeSetup`/`setup` command, the build failed with an error suggesting to configure `stageDependencies`.
Now: text and binary changes are applied by copying the changed files from a filtered Git archive, as the Buildah backend already did. Files changed by user commands are overwritten without an error, and `git apply` edge cases (renames, mode-only changes, whitespace, quoted paths) no longer cause failures.

**Migration:** Audit `install`, `beforeSetup` and `setup` commands that modify files added by `git` mappings: the build no longer stops on such a conflict, and the Git version silently overwrites the modified file. Configure `git.stageDependencies` so that the modifying stage reruns when the source files change, or write generated output outside the `git`-mapped paths.

**References:** [werf#7617](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7617)

#### Stapel import cache depends on the source image, not on checksums of the imported files

<a id="build-import-cache-source-image"></a>`build-import-cache-source-image` · change · `stapel` `cache` · products: werf

Before: by default, the digest of the stage that runs an `import` was calculated from checksums of the files selected by `add`, `includePaths` and `excludePaths`, and werf stored import metadata in the stages storage (and `werf cleanup`/`werf purge` cleaned it). The source-image-based calculation was only available with `WERF_EXPERIMENTAL_IMPORT_BY_SOURCE_IMAGE_TAG=1`.
Now: the digest depends on the content digest of the source image, plus `add`, `to`, `owner`, `group`, `includePaths` and `excludePaths`; the file-checksum mode, the import metadata and the `WERF_EXPERIMENTAL_IMPORT_BY_SOURCE_IMAGE_TAG` variable are gone. Any change of the source image rebuilds the importing image, even if the copied files are unchanged. `werf cleanup` and `werf purge` no longer process import metadata records, so the cleanup report no longer contains `importMetadata` items.

**Migration:** Expect additional rebuilds of images that import files. If they are expensive, put the imported output into a separate, narrowly scoped image and import from it. Remove `WERF_EXPERIMENTAL_IMPORT_BY_SOURCE_IMAGE_TAG` from CI settings.

**References:** [werf@6bab18c00](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/6bab18c00db1), [werf@e36e23740](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/e36e237406f2), [werf@92c88aecc](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/92c88aecc4d3), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#file-imports>

#### The Ansible builder is removed from Stapel

<a id="stapel-ansible-builder-removed"></a>`stapel-ansible-builder-removed` · removal · `stapel` `config` · products: werf

Before: Stapel images could describe build instructions with the `ansible` directive (`ansible.beforeInstall`, `ansible.install`, `ansible.beforeSetup`, `ansible.setup`, `ansible.cacheVersion`, ...), and `WERF_DEBUG_ANSIBLE_ARGS` passed extra arguments to Ansible.
Now: only the Shell builder (`shell`) remains. The `ansible` key in `werf.yaml` is a configuration error, `WERF_DEBUG_ANSIBLE_ARGS` is ignored, and the Stapel container no longer ships Ansible.

**Migration:** Rewrite `ansible:` steps as `shell:` commands (renaming the key is not enough: Ansible modules have to be replaced with equivalent shell commands), or move the image to a Dockerfile.

**References:** [werf@5eba17525](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/5eba1752542f), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#builders-and-image-configuration>

#### The Docker backend requires Docker 19.03 (Engine API 1.40) or newer and fails fast on an unresponsive daemon

<a id="build-docker-api-1-40-required"></a>`build-docker-api-1-40-required` · change · `images` `platform` · products: werf

Before: werf talked to the Docker daemon through a client that negotiated down to older Engine API versions, and a daemon socket that accepted connections but never answered (a stopped Docker Desktop, a dead SSH tunnel) hung the command indefinitely.
Now: werf uses the Docker CLI's Engine client for all Docker operations. Commands that build or run containers (`build`, `converge`, `render`, `plan`, `lint`, `export`, `run`, `kube-run`, `compose`, `bundle publish`, `stage image`, `stages copy`, `host cleanup`, `host purge` and others) fail at backend initialization with `check Docker daemon API: ...` when the daemon advertises an API older than 1.40, and fail after 10s with `Docker daemon did not answer within 10s` when the daemon does not respond. Commands that only talk to registries (`cleanup`, `purge`, `dismiss`, `managed-images`, `meta-repo`) and chart-only `plan`, `lint`, `helm get-autogenerated-values` and `bundle publish` (projects without images, `--without-images`, and for some of them `--stub-tags` or local repo) do not require the daemon. Named Docker contexts and `ssh://` Docker hosts keep working.

**Migration:** Upgrade Docker daemons older than 19.03 before using werf v3 with the Docker backend, or switch to the Buildah backend.

**References:** [werf@b9ca56d9c](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/b9ca56d9c86b), [werf#7973](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7973), [werf#7981](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7981), [werf#7988](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7988)

#### The `--virtual-merge` mode is removed

<a id="build-virtual-merge-removed"></a>`build-virtual-merge-removed` · removal · `git` `cli` · products: werf

Before: `--virtual-merge` (`$WERF_VIRTUAL_MERGE`) in `werf build`, `converge`, `run`, `bundle publish` and other building commands treated the current commit as an ephemeral merge commit (e.g. a CI merge-request merge result) and built git patches relative to its parents.
Now: the flag and the environment variable are removed; the current commit is always used as is.

**Migration:** Remove `--virtual-merge` and `WERF_VIRTUAL_MERGE` from scripts and CI configuration: passing the flag is an error.

**References:** [werf@58dfbbdfe](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/58dfbbdfe248), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#removed-flags-and-modes>

#### The `artifact` image type is removed; use `image` with `final: false`

<a id="stapel-artifact-removed"></a>`stapel-artifact-removed` · removal · `stapel` `config` · products: werf

Before: deprecated `artifact: NAME` documents described Stapel images used only as a source of imports; `fromArtifact` used an artifact as the base image, and `import.artifact` imported files from an artifact.
Now: the `artifact` document, `fromArtifact` and `import.artifact` are no longer supported and are configuration errors. An intermediate image is an ordinary `image` with `final: false`.

**Migration:** Replace `artifact: NAME` with `image: NAME` plus `final: false`, keeping the other settings; replace `fromArtifact: NAME` with `from: NAME` and `import.artifact: NAME` with `import.from: NAME`.

**References:** [werf@8003cbaf3](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/8003cbaf3936), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#images-instead-of-artifacts>

#### The `docker` directive is removed from Stapel images; use `imageSpec.config`

<a id="stapel-docker-directive-removed"></a>`stapel-docker-directive-removed` · removal · `stapel` `config` · products: werf

Before: the deprecated `docker` directive of a Stapel image set image configuration in Dockerfile-instruction terms (`VOLUME`, `EXPOSE`, `ENV`, `LABEL`, `ENTRYPOINT`, `CMD`, `WORKDIR`, `USER`, `HEALTHCHECK`) as a separate `dockerInstructions` stage.
Now: the `docker` key is a configuration error; image configuration is set only with `imageSpec.config`.

**Migration:** Move the settings to `imageSpec.config`, translating names and formats, e.g. `docker.WORKDIR: /app` → `imageSpec.config.workingDir: /app`, `docker.ENV: {A: b}` → `imageSpec.config.env: {A: b}`. Expect the affected images to be rebuilt.

**References:** [werf@13fbe9260](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/13fbe92607c7), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#builders-and-image-configuration>

#### The build report marks whole-image reuse with `StagesSkipped: true` and may omit `Stages`

<a id="build-report-stages-skipped"></a>`build-report-stages-skipped` · change · `build-report` · products: werf

Before: every image record of the JSON build report (`--save-build-report`) had a `Stages` field (possibly `null`).
Now: when an image is reused as a whole by its content-based tag, its record contains `StagesSkipped: true` and no `Stages` field; `Stages` is omitted whenever it is empty. Image-level fields (`DockerTag`, `DockerImageName`, `DockerImageDigest` and others) describe the content-based tag image.

**Migration:** Make parsers of the build report tolerate a missing `Stages` field and do not treat `StagesSkipped: true` as an error or as a sign that the image is not ready.

**References:** [werf#7638](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7638), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#build-report-format>

#### The native Buildah backend honors `network:` and `--backend-network` for Dockerfile images

<a id="build-buildah-dockerfile-network-honored"></a>`build-buildah-dockerfile-network-honored` · change · `buildah` `dockerfile` · products: werf

Before: with the native Buildah backend (`WERF_BUILDAH_MODE=native-chroot` or `native-rootless`), `network:` of a Dockerfile image in `werf.yaml` and `--backend-network` were silently ignored for non-staged Dockerfile builds, and in a rootless build a `RUN` ran in the host network namespace when slirp4netns was absent.
Now: they are honored for non-staged Dockerfile images, and only `default`, `host` and `none` are supported: any other value, such as `bridge` or a named Docker network, fails with `unsupported network mode "bridge" for the native Buildah backend (supported: default, host, none)`. A `RUN` of a rootless Dockerfile build runs in its own network namespace configured by pasta. Images with `staged: true` still ignore the image-level setting; only `RUN --network=` applies there. In `native-chroot` mode Buildah forces host networking, so `network: none` does not isolate a `RUN`. The Docker backend is unchanged.

**Migration:** Review `network:` of Dockerfile images in `werf.yaml` and `--backend-network` (`WERF_BACKEND_NETWORK`) used with the native Buildah backend: replace Docker-specific values (`bridge`, named networks) with `default`, `host` or `none`, or remove them, and check that builds which used to get host networking still have the connectivity they need. Do not rely on `network: none` for isolation in `native-chroot` mode.

**References:** [werf#7730](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7730)

#### The native Buildah backend requires netavark (and pasta for rootless networking) instead of CNI and slirp4netns

<a id="build-buildah-netavark"></a>`build-buildah-netavark` · change · `buildah` `distribution` · products: werf

Before: the native Buildah backend (`WERF_BUILDAH_MODE=native-chroot` or `native-rootless`) used CNI plugins and slirp4netns for container networking.
Now: the backend uses netavark, and backend initialization fails with `could not find "netavark" in one of [...]` when the `netavark` binary is missing from the Podman helper directories (`/usr/local/libexec/podman`, `/usr/local/lib/podman`, `/usr/libexec/podman`, `/usr/lib/podman`), even if no instruction uses the network. A rootless build that configures a network (not `network: host`/`none`, not chroot mode) additionally needs `pasta` from the `passt` package. The official werf images ship `netavark`, `passt` (`pasta`) and `aardvark-dns`; their Alpine base moved from 3.18 to 3.24, the Fedora base from 38 to 44 and the Ubuntu base from 22.04 to 24.04 (the `build` and `build1001` users keep UIDs 1000 and 1001).

**Migration:** With the official werf image, switch to the v3 image (not only the binary) and rebuild images derived from it, checking that packages and commands they add still work on the new Alpine, Fedora or Ubuntu base. With your own installation or image, install the distribution `netavark` package (and `passt` for rootless builds with networking) where werf runs.

**References:** [werf#7730](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7730), [werf#7925](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7925), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#buildah>

#### `--skip-image-spec-stage` is removed; the `imageSpec` stage always runs when configured

<a id="build-skip-image-spec-stage-removed"></a>`build-skip-image-spec-stage-removed` · removal · `cli` `images` · products: werf

Before: the hidden `--skip-image-spec-stage` flag (`$WERF_SKIP_IMAGE_SPEC_STAGE`) skipped the `imageSpec` stage, a workaround for local stages storage.
Now: the flag is removed; passing it is an `unknown flag` error, and `WERF_SKIP_IMAGE_SPEC_STAGE` is ignored. The `imageSpec` stage always runs when `imageSpec` is configured, including with `--repo :local`.

**Migration:** Remove `--skip-image-spec-stage` and `WERF_SKIP_IMAGE_SPEC_STAGE` from scripts. Expect `imageSpec` settings to be applied to images built with local storage.

**References:** [werf#7646](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7646), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#removed-flags-and-modes>

#### `disableGitAfterPatch` is removed

<a id="build-disable-git-after-patch-removed"></a>`build-disable-git-after-patch-removed` · removal · `stapel` `git` `config` · products: werf

Before: `disableGitAfterPatch: true` in a Stapel image froze the Git sources after the patch stage, skipping the `gitCache` and `gitLatestPatch` stages so that later commits did not update the files in the image. v2 suggested it to keep artifact behavior when replacing `artifact` with `image`.
Now: the directive is not supported and is a configuration error. There is no equivalent switch.

**Migration:** Remove `disableGitAfterPatch` from `werf.yaml`. Use `git.stageDependencies` to control which changes rerun build instructions; this does not stop updates of the Git files themselves.

**References:** [werf@55dc5ea4b](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/55dc5ea4b013), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#images-instead-of-artifacts>

#### `git.stageDependencies` for a stage without instructions is an error

<a id="build-stage-dependencies-unused-stage-error"></a>`build-stage-dependencies-unused-stage-error` · change · `stapel` `git` `validation` · products: werf

Before: a non-empty `git.stageDependencies.<stage>` (`install`, `beforeSetup` or `setup`) for a Stapel image with no instructions for that stage only printed a warning, and the masks had no effect.
Now: werf fails with `git.stageDependencies.<stage> is defined, but no <stage> instructions are provided for image "<name>"`.

**Migration:** Move the masks to the stage that has the corresponding commands, add the missing instructions, or remove the unnecessary `stageDependencies` entry.

**References:** [werf#7529](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7529), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#git-dependencies-of-build-stages>

#### `import.stage` is removed; imports always copy from the completed source image

<a id="build-import-stage-removed"></a>`build-import-stage-removed` · removal · `stapel` `config` · products: werf

Before: `import.stage` (`beforeInstall`, `install`, `beforeSetup` or `setup`) selected the stage of the source image to copy files from.
Now: the `stage` key of an import is not supported and is a configuration error; files are always copied from the completed source image. `before`/`after` still control when the import runs in the destination image.

**Migration:** Remove `stage` from every `import` entry. If you need an intermediate result, make it a separate image (`final: false`) and import from it.

**References:** [werf@55dc5ea4b](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/55dc5ea4b013), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#file-imports>

#### `werf build` and `werf config list` default to `--final-images-only=true`

<a id="build-final-images-only-default"></a>`build-final-images-only-default` · change · `cli` `images` · products: werf

Before: `werf build` defaulted to `--final-images-only=false` and built every image of `werf.yaml`, including orphan non-final images (`final: false`) that no final image uses; `werf config list` listed non-final images too and accepted the deprecated `--images-only` alias.
Now: both commands default to `--final-images-only=true`, like `converge`, `render`, `export`, `plan`, `lint` and `bundle publish` already did. `werf build` builds final images and the non-final images they need via `from`, `import` or `dependencies`; orphan non-final images are no longer built. `werf config list` lists only final images, and `--images-only` is removed.

**Migration:** To keep the previous behavior, pass `--final-images-only=false` to `werf build` (or set `WERF_FINAL_IMAGES_ONLY=false`) and to `werf config list`. Replace the removed `--images-only` flag with `--final-images-only`.

**References:** [werf#7618](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7618), [werf#7647](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7647), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#which-images-are-built-and-listed>

#### `werf meta-repo migrate` and `werf meta-repo detach` no longer accept Kubernetes connection flags

<a id="meta-repo-commands-kube-flags-removed"></a>`meta-repo-commands-kube-flags-removed` · removal · `cli` `registry` · products: werf

Before: in werf v2.85.0, `werf meta-repo migrate` and `werf meta-repo detach` accepted `--kube-config`, `--kube-config-base64` and `--kube-context` (`$WERF_KUBE_CONFIG`, `$WERF_KUBE_CONFIG_BASE64`, `$WERF_KUBE_CONTEXT`) and initialized a Kubernetes connection on demand.
Now: these flags are removed from both commands; passing them is an unknown-flag error, and the environment variables are ignored by these commands. The commands still accept `--synchronization`.

**Migration:** Remove `--kube-config`, `--kube-config-base64` and `--kube-context` from `werf meta-repo migrate`/`detach` invocations. With Kubernetes synchronization, put the context and kubeconfig into the address: `--synchronization=kubernetes://NAMESPACE[:CONTEXT][@CONFIG_PATH]`.

**References:** [werf#7739](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7739)

#### werf alone filters the Dockerfile build context and also reads `.containerignore`

<a id="build-context-ignore-files-unified"></a>`build-context-ignore-files-unified` · change · `dockerfile` `buildah` · products: werf

Before: werf filtered the build context with `<dockerfile>.dockerignore` or `.dockerignore`, but the Buildah backend then re-applied the context ignore files on its own: files added by `contextAddFiles` could be stripped again, the context `.dockerignore` could win over a Dockerfile-specific one, and `.containerignore` was honored by Buildah only, not by werf or the Docker backend.
Now: the build context is assembled and filtered only by werf, identically on Docker and Buildah. werf reads ignore files in this order: `<dockerfile>.dockerignore`, `<dockerfile>.containerignore`, `.dockerignore`, `.containerignore`. `.containerignore` files are governed by the same giterminism option as `.dockerignore` (`allowUncommittedDockerignoreFiles`).

**Migration:** If a project has a `.containerignore` but no `.dockerignore`, check its patterns: they now apply on both backends and change the build context and stage digests. On Buildah, check that `contextAddFiles` and Dockerfile-specific ignore files now produce the expected context.

**References:** [werf#7722](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7722)

### Deploy

#### Deploy and delete dependency annotations can wait for resources outside the release

<a id="dependency-annotations-external-auto"></a>`dependency-annotations-external-auto` · feature · `annotations` `plan` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `werf.io/deploy-dependency-<id>` and `werf.io/delete-dependency-<id>` could only point to resources of the release; a dependency that matched no release resource was ignored. Waiting for resources outside the release needed the separate `<id>.external-dependency.werf.io/*` annotations.
Now: both annotations accept `external=auto|true|false` (default `auto`).
- `external=true`, or `auto` when no release resource matches, makes the dependency external: Nelm waits for the resource in the cluster to be `present`/`ready` (deploy) or `absent` (delete). `kind`, `version` and `name` must then be specified, plus `group` for non-core groups and `namespace` if it is not the release namespace.
- `external=false` restricts the dependency to release resources.
- With `external` omitted, a dependency missing `name`, `kind` or `version` is treated as internal, so incomplete annotations, including those stored in older releases, keep working; Nelm warns once when such an internal dependency matches no release resource.
External dependencies are not forced into readiness tracking of release resources.

**Migration:** Check `werf.io/deploy-dependency-*` and `werf.io/delete-dependency-*` annotations that fully specify `kind`, `version` and `name` of a resource that is not in the release: they used to be ignored and now make the deploy or deletion wait for that resource in the cluster. Add `external=false` to keep ignoring it, or remove the annotation.

**References:** [werf#8081](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8081), [werf#8114](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8114), [nelm#617](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/617), [nelm@b4771c646](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/b4771c646ede), [nelm#755](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/755), [nelm#769](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/769)

#### Deploy, rollback and uninstall reports identify their format with `"apiVersion": "v3"`

<a id="deploy-report-api-version"></a>`deploy-report-api-version` · change · `deploy-report` · products: nelm, werf

Before: the JSON reports saved with `--save-report-to` (Nelm) or `--save-deploy-report`, `--save-rollback-report`, `--save-uninstall-report` (werf) had a numeric `"version": 3` field.
Now: the field is replaced with the string `"apiVersion": "v3"`; `version` is no longer written. In the Go API, `ReleaseReportV3.Version int` is replaced with `ReleaseReportV3.APIVersion string`.

**Migration:** Update scripts that read or validate `version` to check `apiVersion == "v3"` instead.

**References:** [nelm#607](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/607)

#### Diffs of Secrets and resources marked `werf.io/sensitive` hide only `data` and `stringData` values

<a id="deploy-sensitive-data-and-stringdata-only"></a>`deploy-sensitive-data-and-stringdata-only` · change · `plan` `annotations` · products: nelm, werf

Before: the whole diff of a `v1/Secret` and of any resource annotated `werf.io/sensitive: "true"` was replaced with `<hidden sensitive changes>`. The selective behavior was opt-in through the `field-sensitive` or `preview-v2` feature gates (`NELM_FEAT_FIELD_SENSITIVE=true`, `NELM_FEAT_PREVIEW_V2=true`).
Now: for such resources only values at `data.*` and `stringData.*` are hidden (replaced with length and hash information); metadata, key names and all other fields are shown in the diff. `werf.io/sensitive-paths` still overrides the default path list. The feature gate is removed.

**Migration:** If a resource keeps sensitive data outside `data`/`stringData` (e.g. in `spec`), annotate it with `werf.io/sensitive-paths` listing the JSONPath expressions to hide, e.g. `"$.spec.token"`; include `$.data.*` and `$.stringData.*` too if needed, since the annotation replaces the default list. Remove `NELM_FEAT_FIELD_SENSITIVE` from the environment.

**References:** [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc)

#### Encrypted secret values keep their YAML type, style and comments

<a id="secrets-yaml-value-types-preserved"></a>`secrets-yaml-value-types-preserved` · change · `secrets` `values` · products: nelm, werf

Before: encrypting a value in a secret values file stored only its text, so every encrypted value was decrypted as a string: `port: 8080` became `port: "8080"`, `enabled: true` became `"true"`. Block scalar style and comments on encrypted values were dropped.
Now: newly encrypted values store their YAML tag and scalar style, so numbers, booleans and other types stay typed after decryption and block scalars keep their style. Changing only the type of a value (e.g. `"8080"` to `8080`) now re-encrypts it. Comments attached to encrypted values are preserved and stay in cleartext in the encrypted file, like keys.
Values encrypted before this change never stored their type: they are still read as strings, and decrypting and encrypting the file again does not restore the type.

**Migration:** Values you newly enter as unquoted numbers or booleans are now passed to templates and `values.schema.json` as numbers or booleans, not strings: quote them if templates expect strings. To give an old value its type, re-enter it with `werf helm secret values edit` / `nelm chart secret values-file edit`. Do not put secrets in comments of secret values files.

**References:** [common-go#37](https://github.com/werf/common-go/pull/37)

#### Helm path environment variables `HELM_CACHE_HOME`, `HELM_CONFIG_HOME`, `HELM_DATA_HOME` and `HELM_REPOSITORY_*` are no longer read

<a id="charts-helm-path-env-vars-ignored"></a>`charts-helm-path-env-vars-ignored` · removal · `charts` `dependencies` · products: nelm, werf

Before: the Helm cache, config and data directories could be moved with `HELM_CACHE_HOME`, `HELM_CONFIG_HOME` and `HELM_DATA_HOME`, and chart download and dependency resolution during render, lint, plan and install also honored `HELM_REPOSITORY_CONFIG`, `HELM_REPOSITORY_CACHE` and `HELM_CONTENT_CACHE`.
Now: `HELM_CACHE_HOME`, `HELM_CONFIG_HOME` and `HELM_DATA_HOME` are ignored everywhere, and render, lint, plan and install commands also ignore `HELM_REPOSITORY_CONFIG`, `HELM_REPOSITORY_CACHE` and `HELM_CONTENT_CACHE` (the Helm-based `nelm chart repo` commands still read them). The chart repository list and the chart caches are located only via `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME` and `XDG_DATA_HOME`, by default `~/.config/helm`, `~/.cache/helm` and `~/.local/share/helm` on Linux. The XDG variables point to the parent directory: with `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/custom/config`, `/custom/config/helm/repositories.yaml` is read.

**Migration:** If you set `HELM_CONFIG_HOME`/`HELM_REPOSITORY_CONFIG` or the cache variables, copy `repositories.yaml` to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/helm/repositories.yaml` (or `~/.config/helm/`) or add the repositories again, and set `XDG_CACHE_HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` instead of the `HELM_*` variables.

**References:** [werf#7518](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7518), [nelm#611](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/611)

#### Installing from a saved plan respects `--release-history-limit`

<a id="plan-use-plan-release-history-limit"></a>`plan-use-plan-release-history-limit` · fix · `plan` `release-storage` `go-api` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `nelm release install --use-plan` (werf: `werf converge --use-plan`) took the release history limit from the saved plan, where it was always `0`, so old release revisions were never pruned and the history grew without limit.
Now: the history limit comes from `--release-history-limit` of the install command (default `10`), as without `--use-plan`.
Go API: `ReleaseHistoryLimit` moved from `common.ReleaseInstallRuntimeOptions` to `action.ReleaseInstallOptions` (as in `ReleaseRollbackOptions` and `ReleaseUninstallOptions`) and is no longer stored in plan artifacts.
In werf, `werf converge --use-plan` and `werf bundle apply --use-plan` now respect `--releases-history-max` (`$WERF_RELEASES_HISTORY_MAX`).

**Migration:** Go API callers that set `ReleaseHistoryLimit` inside a `common.ReleaseInstallRuntimeOptions` literal must set `action.ReleaseInstallOptions.ReleaseHistoryLimit` instead. Releases installed from saved plans may have accumulated many revisions; the next install prunes them down to the limit.

**References:** [werf#8085](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8085), [nelm@65c01393d](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/65c01393de40)

#### Lookalike keys such as `werf-io/weight` no longer act as `werf.io/*` and `helm.sh/*` annotations

<a id="annotations-lookalike-keys-ignored"></a>`annotations-lookalike-keys-ignored` · fix · `annotations` · products: nelm, werf

Before: the patterns for Nelm's annotation and label keys didn't escape the dot, so any character in place of a `.` matched: `werf-io/weight`, `helm-sh/hook`, `werfXio/deploy-dependency-foo` etc. were validated and applied as `werf.io/weight`, `helm.sh/hook` and so on (e.g. `werf-io/weight: "abc"` failed the deploy with `invalid value "abc" for annotation "werf-io/weight"`).
Now: only the exactly spelled `werf.io/*`, `helm.sh/*`, `meta.helm.sh/*` and `app.kubernetes.io/*` keys are recognized; lookalike keys are ignored by Nelm.

**Migration:** If a chart relied on a misspelled key such as `werf-io/weight` or `helm-sh/hook`, rename it to the dotted key (`werf.io/weight`, `helm.sh/hook`).

**References:** [werf#8132](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8132), [nelm#799](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/799)

#### No-op deploy flags are removed from werf commands that ignored them

<a id="cli-werf-noop-deploy-flags-removed"></a>`cli-werf-noop-deploy-flags-removed` · removal · `cli` · products: werf

Before: several werf commands accepted deploy flags that had no effect there:
- `--insecure-helm-dependencies` on `werf build`, `werf bundle copy`, `werf cleanup`, `werf compose *`, `werf dismiss`, `werf export`, `werf managed-images add|ls|rm`, `werf purge`, `werf run` and `werf stage image`;
- `--hooks-status-progress-period` on `werf converge`, `werf bundle apply`, `werf dismiss`, `werf rollback`, `werf plan` and `werf render`;
- `--status-progress-period` and `--releases-history-max` on `werf plan` and `werf render`;
- `--timeout`/`-t` on `werf plan`.
Now: these flags are removed from those commands; passing them is an unknown-flag error. Commands where the flags work (for example `--insecure-helm-dependencies` on `werf converge`, `--status-progress-period` and `--releases-history-max` on `werf converge`) keep them.

**Migration:** Remove the listed flags from invocations of the listed commands. The corresponding `WERF_*` environment variables are simply ignored there.

**References:** [werf@0b50bd1bb](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/0b50bd1bbf42)

#### Non-string annotation and label values fail rendering instead of being dropped

<a id="render-invalid-annotations-labels-fail"></a>`render-invalid-annotations-labels-fail` · change · `render` `validation` `annotations` · products: nelm, werf

Before: entries of `metadata.annotations` and `metadata.labels` in chart manifests whose value was not a string (e.g. an unquoted number or boolean) were dropped with a warning, and the resource was deployed without them.
Now: such a value fails rendering, linting, planning and installing with a `decode resource (file: "..."): ...` error. Resources already stored in a release are not rejected: their invalid entries are dropped with a warning. Go API users can restore the old behavior with the new `DropInvalidAnnotationsAndLabels` option of `ChartRenderOptions`, `ChartLintOptions`, `ReleaseInstallOptions` and `ReleasePlanInstallOptions`.

**Migration:** Quote numbers and booleans in annotations and labels in templates, e.g. `example.com/replicas: "3"` or `{{ .Values.x | quote }}`.

**References:** [nelm#614](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/614)

#### Null fields are removed from rendered manifests by default

<a id="deploy-null-fields-cleaned-by-default"></a>`deploy-null-fields-cleaned-by-default` · change · `render` `resources` · products: nelm, werf

Before: fields and list entries with a `null` value were kept in rendered manifests and sent to the cluster as is. Removing them was opt-in through the `clean-null-fields` or `preview-v2` feature gates (`NELM_FEAT_CLEAN_NULL_FIELDS=true`, `NELM_FEAT_PREVIEW_V2=true`).
Now: `null` fields and list entries are removed recursively from all rendered resources, as Helm does, both for deploy and for the manifests printed by `render` commands. The feature gate is removed and there is no switch to restore the previous behavior.

**Migration:** Check resources that intentionally set a field to `null` (an absent field and an explicit `null` are not always equivalent for Kubernetes and CRDs) and set an explicit value instead. Remove `NELM_FEAT_CLEAN_NULL_FIELDS` from the environment.

**References:** [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc), [nelm@e9bbd6e25](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/e9bbd6e25a02)

#### OCI charts are pulled by one manifest digest with stricter provenance verification

<a id="charts-oci-pull-digest-pinned"></a>`charts-oci-pull-digest-pinned` · change · `charts` `oci` `registry` · products: nelm, werf

Changes for remote `oci://` charts in `release install`, `release plan install`, `chart render`, `chart lint` and `chart download`:
- A tag is resolved to a manifest digest once, and the chart and its provenance are fetched by that digest (the provenance never comes from a cache). The resolved digest is logged (`Resolved chart … to digest …`, and `Verified chart … signed by …` after verification).
- With `--provenance-strategy` `verify` or `verify-if-possible`, a semver tag (leading `v` dropped, `_` read as `+`) must equal the chart version; `verify` without `--provenance-keyring` fails before downloading, and a signed chart under `verify-if-possible` without a keyring fails. A tag ending in `.prov` is rejected.
- An OCI chart can be pulled by an existing non-semver tag (e.g. `oci://repo/chart:latest`).
- Install, plan, render and lint download charts into a private per-invocation directory that is removed afterwards, not into Helm's shared repository cache.
- Nelm: in install, plan, render and lint, `--chart-repo-ca`, `--chart-repo-cert`/`--chart-repo-key`, `--no-verify-chart-repos-tls` and `--chart-repo-request-timeout` now apply to `oci://` charts; basic-auth credentials are sent only to the chart's host. `nelm chart download` keeps Helm's flags (`--ca-file`, `--cert-file`, `--key-file`, `--insecure-skip-tls-verify`, `--plain-http`). Loopback registries (`localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`) are reached over plain HTTP unless TLS options are given; with `--insecure-chart-repos` plain HTTP is always used.
- werf: bundles are pulled with `--insecure-registry` (plain HTTP) and `--skip-tls-verify-registry`; dependency charts use `--skip-tls-verify-helm-dependencies`. werf has no option for a custom CA file.

**Migration:** If you verify provenance of OCI charts, make sure the tag you deploy equals the chart version (or deploy by digest) and pass `--provenance-keyring`. For OCI registries with self-signed certificates, pass the CA with `--chart-repo-ca` in Nelm (`--ca-file` for `nelm chart download`); in werf, add the CA to the system trust store, or as a last resort use `--skip-tls-verify-registry` (bundles) or `--skip-tls-verify-helm-dependencies` (dependencies).

**References:** [werf#8144](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8144), [nelm#811](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/811)

#### Offline rendering assumes Kubernetes 1.36.0 by default

<a id="render-default-kube-version-1-36"></a>`render-default-kube-version-1-36` · change · `render` · products: nelm, werf

Before: without cluster access (`nelm chart render`, `nelm chart lint`, `werf render`, `werf lint`, `werf bundle render`), `.Capabilities.KubeVersion` defaulted to `1.20.0`.
Now: the default is `1.36.0`. Templates that branch on `.Capabilities.KubeVersion` (e.g. choose API versions) may render differently.

**Migration:** Pass `--kube-version 1.20.0` to keep the previous rendering, or update the templates.

**References:** [nelm@2159f9621](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/2159f962147e)

#### Packed charts keep their publish-time inputs in `.werf-data/` and are deployed as if those inputs were passed again

<a id="charts-werf-data-publish-inputs"></a>`charts-werf-data-publish-inputs` · change · `charts` `values` `bundles` · products: nelm, werf

New: `nelm chart pack` (and `werf bundle publish`, which uses the same code) stores the inputs given at pack time in a `.werf-data/` directory at the chart root, next to the unchanged chart files: `metadata.yaml` (`--set*` options, `--set-root-json`, patches, disable switches such as `--no-default-values`, annotations and labels, release name and namespace), `values.yaml` (merged `--values` files), `secret-values.yaml` (merged `--secret-values` files, still encrypted), `extra-values.yaml` (service values, e.g. werf's) and `set-files/` (`--set-file` contents). Helm, Argo CD and Flux ignore the directory and install the chart with its own values.
Install, plan, render and lint of such a chart replay these inputs as values layers, so the result and the stored release values are the same as deploying the source chart with the pack-time flags: chart values < chart secret values < pack-time `--values` < `--secret-values` < `--set*` < extra values < deploy-time `--values` < `--secret-values` < `--set*` < service values. Deploy-time `--set*` patch the result of pack-time `--set*`. Pack-time patches are applied between the chart's `patches.yaml` and `--patches`; pack-time annotations and labels are merged below the deploy-time ones. A dependency with its own `.werf-data/` renders like that chart deployed alone, under the parent's values. One info line lists what was loaded from `.werf-data/`.
An empty release name or namespace of `release install`, `release plan install`, `chart render` and `chart lint` is taken from the release recorded in `.werf-data/metadata.yaml`; `--release`/`--namespace` of `release install` and `release plan install` are therefore optional and fail with `release name and release namespace required: not given and not recorded in the chart's .werf-data` only when neither is available. Charts packed by an older format (legacy werf bundles) get the annotations and labels of their `extra_annotations.json`/`extra_labels.json`.
A chart whose `.werf-data/metadata.yaml` has an unknown `apiVersion` fails with `this chart requires a newer Nelm version`.
Old clients: werf v2.85.0 refuses such a chart with `it requires werf v3 or Nelm v2, or newer` (werf/werf#8141). Nelm v1.31.3 and werf v2.84.1 and earlier do not know `.werf-data/` and deploy it without its publish-time inputs (no image values, publish-time values, secrets or annotations), without an error; the same check for Nelm v1 (werf/nelm#808) is not released yet.
werf bundles:
Before: `werf bundle publish` merged the image values, the publish-time `--values`, `--set*` and service values into `values.yaml` of the published chart and the chart and `--secret-values` secret values into its `secret-values.yaml`, and saved annotations and labels in `extra_annotations.json`/`extra_labels.json`. Because the inputs were flattened, a published bundle could render differently from `werf converge` with the same flags (export/import-values, `--set` patching, nulls, `--set-json` replacements, disabled default secrets).
Now: the chart is published unchanged (`Chart.yaml` keeps comments and order; only `name`, `version` and the `helm.sh/images` annotation with the built images and digests are set, and a missing `apiVersion` becomes `v2`). Everything werf adds is stored in `.werf-data/` of the chart: `--values`, `--secret-values` (still encrypted), `--set*`, `--set-file` contents, `--set-root-json`, `--patches`, the disable switches, the image/repo/env/commit service values, annotations and labels, and the release name and namespace. `werf bundle apply`, `werf bundle plan` and `werf bundle render` replay them as values layers, so the result and the stored release values match `werf converge`; `.Chart.Name` and `.Chart.Version` (repository basename, version from the tag) are the known difference.
- Helm, Argo CD and Flux installing a published bundle get only the chart's own `values.yaml`: no image values, publish-time values, secrets or annotations.
- werf v2 cannot deploy the new bundles: werf v2.85.0 refuses them, werf v2.84.1 and earlier deploy them without images and publish-time values. Bundles published by werf v2 are still deployed by werf v3 unchanged, except that for them the annotations passed to `werf bundle apply`/`plan`/`render` (`--add-annotation`, werf service annotations such as `project.werf.io/env`) now win per key over the bundle's `extra_annotations.json`; before, the bundle's `project.werf.io/*`, `ci.werf.io/*` and `werf.io/release-channel` won.
- Publish-time `--secret-values` are saved decrypted in the release at apply, like `werf converge --secret-values`, so `werf release get --print-values` shows them; the first apply of a new bundle over an old release creates a new revision.
- `--disable-default-values` and `--disable-default-secret-values` of `werf bundle apply` ignore only the chart's own files, not the values stored at publish. Disable switches recorded in a committed `.werf-data/metadata.yaml` (e.g. an unpacked published chart committed as `.helm`) are kept by `werf bundle publish` and can only be cleared by editing that file.
- New `werf bundle publish` options: `--patches` and `--no-default-patches`.
- `--tag` of `werf bundle publish`: a strict semver tag (a leading `v` dropped) is the chart version, anything else gives `0.0.0-<unix time>-<tag slug>` (at most 128 characters); the chart is pushed under the version tag and, if different, under the literal tag (`+` pushed as `_`). Publish refuses a tag that equals a werf image tag in the same repository.
- Without `--release`/`--namespace`, `werf bundle apply`/`plan`/`render` use the ones recorded at publish, unless a non-empty `--env` differs from the publish-time env; then both flags are required.
- `--provenance-strategy=verify`/`verify-if-possible` verify bundles pulled from a registry; `verify` with `--bundle-dir` fails.
- `werf converge`, `werf render`, `werf plan` and `werf lint` honor a committed `.helm/.werf-data/`; `.werf-data/` is never excluded by `.helmignore`. A werf-published chart used as a dependency gets its publish-time values folded into its defaults; its annotations, labels, patches and release defaults are ignored with a warning.
- Bundles of charts with `apiVersion: v3` fail with `werf bundle commands don't support Chart.yaml apiVersion v3 yet`.
Go API: `action.ChartPack`, `action.ResolveRecordedRelease`, `chart.DownloadChart`, `*action.ReleaseRequiredError`; the loaded chart gets `WerfDataFiles`.

**Migration:** Upgrade every Nelm and werf that installs, plans, renders or lints published charts or bundles (Nelm v2, werf v3) before publishing with `nelm chart pack` or werf v3 `werf bundle publish`: do not rely on old clients failing. Rename an unrelated existing `.werf-data/` directory at the chart root: it is now interpreted as publish-time inputs and never excluded by `.helmignore`.
werf: When installing published bundles with Helm, Argo CD or Flux, pass `.werf-data/values.yaml` and `.werf-data/extra-values.yaml` as values files (publish-time `--set*` and secrets stay unavailable to them). Pass `--release`/`--namespace` when applying a bundle with a different `--env` than at publish. Expect one new revision on the first apply of a bundle that uses `--secret-values`.

**References:** [werf#8142](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8142), [werf#8144](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8144), [werf#8159](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8159), [nelm#809](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/809), [nelm#811](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/811), [nelm#823](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/823), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#charts-and-bundles>

#### Plan with `--exit-code` returns 3 when only the release needs to be installed

<a id="plan-detailed-exit-code"></a>`plan-detailed-exit-code` · change · `plan` `cli` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `nelm release plan install --exit-code`, `werf plan --exit-code` and `werf bundle plan --exit-code` returned `2` for any planned change, including a release-only update with no resource changes. The extended codes were opt-in through the `more-detailed-exit-code-for-plan` or `preview-v2` feature gates.
Now: exit codes are `0` — no changes, `1` — error, `2` — resource changes planned, `3` — no resource changes, but the release still has to be installed. The feature gate is removed.

**Migration:** Update CI that only accepts `0` and `2` to also handle `3` (not an error, but the release still needs installing). Remove `NELM_FEAT_MORE_DETAILED_EXIT_CODE_FOR_PLAN` from the environment.

**References:** [werf@0b50bd1bb](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/0b50bd1bbf42), [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc)

#### Published bundles are always named after the repository; `--helm-compatible-chart` and `--rename-chart` are removed

<a id="bundle-chart-name-from-repository"></a>`bundle-chart-name-from-repository` · change · `bundles` `charts` · products: werf

Before: `werf bundle publish` kept the chart name from `Chart.yaml` by default (`--helm-compatible-chart`/`-C`, `$WERF_HELM_COMPATIBLE_CHART`, defaulted to `false` there, but to `true` in `werf bundle copy`), and `--rename-chart` (`$WERF_RENAME_CHART`) set an arbitrary name.
Now: `werf bundle publish` and `werf bundle copy` always set the chart name in `Chart.yaml` of the published chart to the last path component of the repository (`REPO` for `REGISTRY/PATH/TO/REPO`), as Helm requires for OCI charts. `--helm-compatible-chart`, `--rename-chart` and their environment variables are removed. `.Chart.Name` and template paths of the published chart change accordingly.

**Migration:** Remove `--helm-compatible-chart`, `-C`, `--rename-chart`, `WERF_HELM_COMPATIBLE_CHART` and `WERF_RENAME_CHART` from scripts. Check templates that depend on `.Chart.Name` (e.g. resource names or `include` of templates by path), or publish to a repository named after the chart.

**References:** [werf@2bd5438fd](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/2bd5438fd681), [werf#8142](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8142), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#charts-and-bundles>

#### Readiness tracking matches status condition types of custom resources case-insensitively

<a id="tracking-condition-types-case-insensitive"></a>`tracking-condition-types-case-insensitive` · change · `tracking` · products: nelm, werf

Before: the built-in readiness rules for custom resources only matched lowercase condition types in `status.conditions` (`ready`, `available`, ...). A resource with a CamelCase condition such as `Ready` or `Available` matched no rule and was reported ready as soon as it appeared. Case-insensitive matching was available only as an opt-in through the `case-insensitive-condition-tracking` feature gate (`NELM_FEAT_CASE_INSENSITIVE_CONDITION_TRACKING=true`).
Now: condition types are always matched case-insensitively, CamelCase first. A custom resource with a `Ready`/`Available` condition is reported ready only once that condition is `True`, so deploys wait for it and may time out if it never becomes `True`. The feature gate is removed; `NELM_FEAT_CASE_INSENSITIVE_CONDITION_TRACKING` is reported as an unsupported environment variable.

**Migration:** Check custom resources that have `Ready` or `Available` conditions: the deploy now waits for them. If a resource never reaches `True` and should not block the deploy, set `werf.io/track-termination-mode: NonBlocking` on it, or fix its controller. Remove `NELM_FEAT_CASE_INSENSITIVE_CONDITION_TRACKING` from the environment.

**References:** [werf#7805](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7805), [nelm@0585a1f40](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/0585a1f4041e), [nelm@ca3aa25c8](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/ca3aa25c8f4f), [kubedog@e8f61a4bc](https://github.com/werf/kubedog/commit/e8f61a4bc90a), [kubedog@438ef109f](https://github.com/werf/kubedog/commit/438ef109f804)

#### Render and diff patches modify rendered resources and drift detection with jq

<a id="resource-patches"></a>`resource-patches` · feature · `patches` `render` · products: nelm, werf

New: rendered resources can be patched with jq programs, from `patches.yaml` in the root of the chart and its subcharts (read automatically) and from files passed with `--patches`. Two kinds of patches:
- `renderPatches` modify resources after rendering and before deploy, like Helm's `--post-renderer`, e.g. to change what a third-party subchart doesn't let you configure. A render patch can't change `apiVersion`, `kind`, `name` or `namespace`, and can read `$Values`, `$Release`, `$Chart` and `$Capabilities` — the same data the templates of the chart that ships `patches.yaml` see (the top-level chart for `--patches` files).
- `diffPatches` don't change what is deployed: they are applied to both the live and the to-be version of a resource when deciding whether to update it, so changes in the patched fields are ignored.
Each rule has a `match` (kinds, groups, versions, names, namespaces, labels, annotations, `charts`; `/.../` values are regular expressions) and a `patch`. `patches.yaml` applies only to resources of its chart and subcharts; `--patches` files apply to all resources. Patches are applied in order, each to the result of the previous one: subcharts, then the parent chart, then `--patches` files. `release rollback` and `release uninstall` apply only diff patches. jq `debug` and `debug(msg)` print to the log at `--log-level debug` or `trace`, naming the patch rule and resource.
`--no-default-patches` ignores `patches.yaml` of all charts.
Go API: `LegacyPatches` (`spec.Patches`) on render, lint, install, plan install, rollback and uninstall options passes rules programmatically, applied after `PatchesFiles`.
In werf, `werf converge`, `werf plan`, `werf render`, `werf lint`, `werf rollback`, `werf dismiss`, `werf bundle apply`, `werf bundle plan` and `werf bundle render` accept `--patches` (`$WERF_PATCHES`, `$WERF_PATCHES_*`) and `--no-default-patches` (`$WERF_NO_DEFAULT_PATCHES`).

**Migration:** A `patches.yaml` file in the root of a chart or subchart is now read automatically. If your chart has a file with this name that serves another purpose, rename it or pass `--no-default-patches` (`WERF_NO_DEFAULT_PATCHES=true` in werf); otherwise it may change manifests or fail the deploy.

**References:** [werf#7661](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7661), [werf#7735](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7735), [werf#7815](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7815), [werf#7958](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7958), [nelm@9241ea8a5](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/9241ea8a51d0), [nelm#696](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/696), [nelm#720](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/720), [nelm#727](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/727), [nelm#785](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/785)

#### Rendered manifests are ordered CRDs first, then all other resources by kind and name

<a id="render-resource-output-order"></a>`render-resource-output-order` · change · `render` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `nelm chart render`, `werf render` and `werf bundle render` printed standalone CRDs (from `crds/`) first, then all `helm.sh/hook` resources, then the regular resources, each group sorted by kind, group, version, namespace and name.
Now: all CRDs (from `crds/`, templates or hooks) come first, then all other resources, hooks and regular resources together, sorted by kind, group, version, namespace and name. The set of rendered resources and their content are unchanged.

**Migration:** If a script relies on the position of hooks in the render output (e.g. compares it with a saved copy), regenerate the saved copy or select resources by their annotations instead of their position.

**References:** [nelm@55bc4628d](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/55bc4628d79e)

#### Resource validation uses Kubernetes and CRD schemas embedded into the binary

<a id="resource-validation-embedded-schemas"></a>`resource-validation-embedded-schemas` · change · `validation` · products: nelm, werf
