Before: resource validation downloaded JSON schemas from the network (`--resource-validation-schema`, by default the `yannh/kubernetes-json-schema` and `datreeio/CRDs-catalog` repositories) for one Kubernetes version (`--resource-validation-kube-version`, default `1.35.0`); `--local-resource-validation` disabled the network sources.
Now: the Kubernetes schemas of the last five Kubernetes minor versions (merged, newest wins) and the `datreeio/CRDs-catalog` CRD schemas are embedded into the binary, so validation works offline. A resource kind without a schema is skipped. `--resource-validation-extra-schema` adds schema sources that take precedence over the embedded ones. The `--resource-validation-schema`, `--resource-validation-kube-version` and `--local-resource-validation` flags are removed. The embedded schemas are refreshed with new releases.

**Migration:** Remove `--resource-validation-schema`, `--resource-validation-kube-version` and `--local-resource-validation` (and their environment variables) from your scripts. To validate against your own schemas, pass them with `--resource-validation-extra-schema`.

**References:** [werf#7729](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7729), [werf#7760](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7760), [nelm#673](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/673), [nelm@9d049189c](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/9d049189ce4e), [nelm#778](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/778)

#### Resources are deleted with Background propagation by default

<a id="deploy-delete-propagation-background"></a>`deploy-delete-propagation-background` · change · `resources` `uninstall` · products: nelm, werf

Before: resources were deleted with `Foreground` propagation: deletion of a resource (e.g. a Deployment) finished only after its dependents (ReplicaSets, Pods) were gone.
Now: the default is `Background`: the resource is deleted immediately and its dependents are garbage-collected afterwards, so subsequent steps no longer wait for them. This applies to deletion during install, rollback and uninstall, and to recreation of resources.

**Migration:** If a later step depends on dependents being gone, set the `werf.io/delete-propagation: Foreground` annotation on the resource, or pass `--delete-propagation=Foreground` (`NELM_DELETE_PROPAGATION` / `WERF_DELETE_PROPAGATION`).

**References:** [nelm#623](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/623)

#### Resources are validated against Kubernetes JSON schemas by default

<a id="resource-validation-enabled-by-default"></a>`resource-validation-enabled-by-default` · change · `validation` `resources` · products: nelm, werf

Before: validating rendered resources against Kubernetes JSON schemas, and the `--no-resource-validation`, `--resource-validation-*` flags, were available only with the `resource-validation` feature gate (`NELM_FEAT_RESOURCE_VALIDATION=true`).
Now: resource validation is on by default in `nelm release install`, `nelm release plan install`, `nelm release rollback` and `nelm chart lint`, and in `werf converge`, `werf plan`, `werf rollback`, `werf lint`, `werf bundle apply` and `werf bundle plan`; manifests that do not match the schema of their kind are rejected before being applied. The `--no-resource-validation`, `--resource-validation-skip`, `--resource-validation-extra-schema` and `--resource-validation-cache-lifetime` flags are always available. The feature gate is removed. Render commands (`nelm chart render`, `werf render`, `werf bundle render`) do not run this validation: use lint to check resources against the schemas.

**Migration:** Fix resources that fail validation. Skip specific resources with `--resource-validation-skip` (e.g. `kind=MyKind`), add schemas for custom resources with `--resource-validation-extra-schema`, or disable validation entirely with `--no-resource-validation`. Remove `NELM_FEAT_RESOURCE_VALIDATION` from the environment.

**References:** [werf@0b50bd1bb](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/0b50bd1bbf42), [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc)

#### Runtime annotations and labels appear in rendered manifests and changes to them alone do not update resources

<a id="render-runtime-annotations-and-labels"></a>`render-runtime-annotations-and-labels` · change · `render` `annotations` `plan` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `nelm chart render` and `werf render`/`werf bundle render` ignored runtime annotations: `--runtime-annotations` of Nelm and werf's service annotations (`werf.io/version`, `project.werf.io/name`, `project.werf.io/env`, `ci.werf.io/*`, `werf.io/release-channel`) were not in the output. During install, plan and rollback, only werf's own service annotations were ignored when deciding whether a resource needs an update; a change in the value of a custom `--runtime-annotations`/`--runtime-labels` entry alone triggered an update.
Now: runtime annotations and labels (`--runtime-annotations`, `--runtime-labels` in Nelm; the service annotations in werf) are added to the rendered manifests. Install, plan and rollback ignore all runtime annotations and labels when deciding whether a live resource differs from the chart, so changing only their values does not update resources; they are applied together with other changes.

**Migration:** If you compare render output with saved manifests or feed it to other tools, expect the additional runtime annotations and labels (in werf: `werf.io/version`, `project.werf.io/name`, `project.werf.io/env` and others). Use regular `--annotations`/`--labels` (werf: `--add-annotation`/`--add-label`) for metadata whose change must update resources.

**References:** [nelm#615](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/615)

#### SQL release storage keeps release annotations in a new `nelm_release_annotations_v1` table

<a id="release-storage-sql-annotations-table"></a>`release-storage-sql-annotations-table` · change · `release-storage` · products: nelm, werf

Before: SQL (PostgreSQL) release storage used only Helm's `releases_v1` table and the `gorp_migrations` table.
Now: on first use Nelm runs an extra migration, recorded in a new `nelm_migrations` table, which creates the `nelm_release_annotations_v1` table (release annotations, referencing `releases_v1` with `ON DELETE CASCADE`), grants `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` on it and `SELECT` on `nelm_migrations` to `PUBLIC`, and enables row-level security on it. Release annotations are written there in the same transaction as the release and read from it without loading release bodies; the annotations are still kept in the release body for Helm compatibility. If the table can't be read, annotations are read from the body. A write denied by permissions fails with `access to table "nelm_release_annotations_v1" for release namespace "<ns>": check the current role's table privileges and row-level security (RLS) policies`.

**Migration:** If Nelm/werf connects to PostgreSQL with a role that can't create tables, run the first deploy of the new version with a role that can (or apply the migration as a database administrator), so that `nelm_migrations` and `nelm_release_annotations_v1` are created. Row-level security is enabled on `nelm_release_annotations_v1` without policies, so a role that doesn't own the table can't access its rows: create RLS policies for the roles that deploy releases, e.g. per release namespace, matching the policies you use for `releases_v1`.

**References:** [werf#8084](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8084), [nelm#752](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/752)

#### Saved plan artifacts use format `v2`, plans saved by the previous version are rejected

<a id="plan-artifact-format-v2"></a>`plan-artifact-format-v2` · change · `plan` · products: nelm, werf

Before: the plan file written by `nelm release plan install --save-plan` (werf: `werf plan --save-plan`) had `apiVersion: v1` and stored the release in the Helm 3 release format; the version was not checked on `--use-plan`.
Now: the plan file has `apiVersion: v2` and stores the release in a format that also covers `apiVersion: v3` charts. `nelm release install --use-plan`, `nelm release plan show` and `werf converge --use-plan` reject a plan file of another version with `plan artifact <version> is not supported by the current version`.

**Migration:** Do not carry plan files across the upgrade: re-run `plan --save-plan` with the new version before applying.

**References:** [nelm@ae98e045c](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/ae98e045c538)

#### Secrets are encrypted with authenticated AES-GCM that older versions cannot decrypt

<a id="secrets-authenticated-encryption-format"></a>`secrets-authenticated-encryption-format` · change · `secrets` · products: nelm, werf

Before: secret values files (`secret-values.yaml`) and secret files were encrypted with AES-CBC without an integrity check: a corrupted or modified ciphertext could decrypt to garbage, and a wrong secret key was often accepted.
Now: everything that is written (`werf helm secret values edit`/`encrypt`, `werf helm secret file edit`/`encrypt`, `nelm chart secret values-file edit`/`encrypt`, `nelm chart secret file edit`/`encrypt`, and release plans saved with a secret key) uses authenticated AES-GCM: format version 2 for whole files, version 3 for individual YAML values. Tampering and wrong keys are reported as errors. Values encrypted in the old AES-CBC format are still decrypted as before, and the secret key format is unchanged. There is no option to write the old format.
Older werf and Nelm versions cannot decrypt the new format and fail, e.g. with a `decode file ...` error. When only some values of a file are edited, only those values are re-encrypted; the others keep the old format.

**Migration:** Before the first `edit` or `encrypt` with werf v3 / Nelm v2, upgrade every environment that reads the repository's secrets: developer machines, CI jobs, and jobs that apply saved release plans. After secrets are re-encrypted, an old werf or Nelm must not handle the repository; switching back does not restore the old format.

**References:** [werf#7818](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7818), [nelm#706](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/706), [common-go#37](https://github.com/werf/common-go/pull/37)

#### The `--set-runtime-json` option and `$.Runtime` are removed

<a id="values-set-runtime-json-removed"></a>`values-set-runtime-json-removed` · removal · `values` `cli` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `--set-runtime-json` (`$NELM_SET_RUNTIME_JSON`, werf: `$WERF_SET_RUNTIME_JSON`) set keys under `$.Runtime`, available in chart templates.
Now: the option is removed and `$.Runtime` is no longer populated in templates.

**Migration:** Pass the data as values with `--set-json` and read it from `.Values` in templates. Remove `--set-runtime-json` from scripts: an unknown flag fails argument parsing.

**References:** [werf@0b50bd1bb](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/0b50bd1bbf42), [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc)

#### The `--show-verbose-diffs` option is removed, diffs of created and deleted resources are always shown

<a id="plan-show-verbose-diffs-removed"></a>`plan-show-verbose-diffs-removed` · removal · `plan` `cli` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `nelm release plan install`, `nelm release plan show`, `werf plan` and `werf bundle plan` had `--show-verbose-diffs` (default `true`); with `false`, diffs of created and deleted resources were replaced with `<hidden verbose changes>`.
Now: the option is removed and full diffs of created and deleted resources are always shown.

**Migration:** Remove `--show-verbose-diffs` and `WERF_SHOW_VERBOSE_DIFFS`/`NELM_*_SHOW_VERBOSE_DIFFS` from scripts: an unknown flag fails argument parsing.

**References:** [werf@0b50bd1bb](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/0b50bd1bbf42), [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc)

#### The `<id>.external-dependency.werf.io/resource` and `/namespace` annotations are removed

<a id="annotations-external-dependency-removed"></a>`annotations-external-dependency-removed` · removal · `annotations` `tracking` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `<id>.external-dependency.werf.io/resource: <kind>[.<version>.<group>]/<name>` together with `<id>.external-dependency.werf.io/namespace` made a resource wait until a resource outside the release was present and ready. The undocumented `<id>.external-dependency.werf.io: <apiVersion>:<kind>[:<namespace>]:<name>` form worked too.
Now: these annotations are not supported: a warning `annotation "..." in resource "..." is no longer supported, use "werf.io/deploy-dependency-<id>" or "werf.io/delete-dependency-<id>" instead` is printed and the resource does not wait for the external resource.

**Migration:** Replace them with `werf.io/deploy-dependency-<id>`, specifying `kind`, `version`, `name`, `group` for a resource of a non-core group, and `namespace` if it differs from the release namespace, e.g. `secret.external-dependency.werf.io/resource: secret/my-vault-secret` + `secret.external-dependency.werf.io/namespace: vault` become `werf.io/deploy-dependency-secret: state=ready,kind=Secret,version=v1,name=my-vault-secret,namespace=vault,external=true`.

**References:** [nelm#625](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/625)

#### The deprecated `<name>.dependency.werf.io` annotation is removed

<a id="annotations-legacy-dependency-werf-io-removed"></a>`annotations-legacy-dependency-werf-io-removed` · removal · `annotations` · products: nelm, werf

Before: an undocumented, deprecated `<name>.dependency.werf.io: <apiVersion>:<kind>[:<namespace>]:<name>` annotation made the resource wait until the given release resource was present.
Now: the annotation is ignored without a warning.

**Migration:** Replace it with `werf.io/deploy-dependency-<name>: state=present,kind=<kind>,version=<version>[,group=<group>],name=<name>[,namespace=<namespace>]`.

**References:** [nelm@be2f6f8e2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/be2f6f8e20d6)

#### The embedded Helm is upgraded from Helm 3 to Helm 4

<a id="helm-v4-engine"></a>`helm-v4-engine` · change · `charts` `templates` `render` · products: nelm, werf

Before: Nelm embedded a fork of Helm 3 for chart loading, values processing, template rendering, chart repositories and registries.
Now: the embedded fork is based on Helm 4 (v4.2.0): chart loading, values coalescing, `export-values`/`import-values`, the template engine and the chart, repository and registry code follow Helm 4. Root context keys passed with `--set-root-json` still reach templates of the root chart and all subcharts; they can't override the built-in `.Chart`, `.Values`, `.Release`, `.Capabilities`, `.Files` and `.Subcharts`.

**Migration:** Render your charts with the new version and compare the result before deploying: template functions, values coalescing and chart loading follow Helm 4 behavior. See the Helm 4 release notes for changes of the Helm engine.

**References:** [werf@301c8f90d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/301c8f90d859), [werf#7793](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7793), [werf#8027](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8027), [werf#8028](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8028), [nelm@961ca04a4](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/961ca04a485a), [nelm@1e1068f13](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/1e1068f13d24), [nelm#627](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/627), [nelm#686](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/686), [nelm#688](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/688), [nelm#743](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/743), [nelm#742](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/742), [nelm@5416f8667](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/5416f866760c)

#### The no-op `--force-adoption` option is removed from render commands

<a id="render-force-adoption-removed"></a>`render-force-adoption-removed` · removal · `render` `cli` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `nelm chart render`, `werf render` and `werf bundle render` accepted `--force-adoption` (`$NELM_FORCE_ADOPTION`, `$NELM_CHART_RENDER_FORCE_ADOPTION`, `$WERF_FORCE_ADOPTION`), which had no effect there.
Now: the option is removed from these commands. Install, plan and rollback commands keep it.

**Migration:** Remove `--force-adoption` from render invocations: an unknown flag fails argument parsing.

**References:** [werf@0b50bd1bb](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/0b50bd1bbf42), [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc)

#### TypeScript charts are enabled by default and render with Node.js 26+ from the host

<a id="typescript-charts"></a>`typescript-charts` · change · `typescript` `templates` · products: nelm, werf

Before: TypeScript charts (the `ts/` directory of a chart, rendered in addition to or instead of `templates/`) were behind the `NELM_FEAT_TYPESCRIPT=true` feature gate; without it `ts/` was ignored and `chart ts init`/`chart ts build` failed. They were bundled and rendered with Deno 2.7.1, downloaded from GitHub on first use, with `@nelm/chart-ts-sdk` 0.1.x; `--deno-binary-path` (`$NELM_DENO_BINARY_PATH`, `$WERF_DENO_BINARY_PATH`) set an explicit Deno binary.
Now: TypeScript charts are always enabled: a chart with `ts/src` gets its TypeScript manifests rendered, and `chart ts init`, `chart ts build` and `chart pack` (werf: `werf chart ts init`, `werf chart ts build`, `werf bundle publish`) bundle TypeScript without any environment variable. No JavaScript runtime is embedded or downloaded:
- `ts/dist/bundle.js` is built in-process with esbuild (`format: esm`, `platform: node`, `target: node26`); the chart's npm dependencies are installed with the package manager of its lock file (npm, pnpm, yarn or bun) from `PATH`, with package scripts disabled. CommonJS dependencies (kubernetes-models, cdk8s and others) work.
- Rendering, including deploying an already packaged chart, needs Node.js >= 26 from `PATH` or `--node-binary-path` (`$NELM_NODE_BINARY_PATH`, `$WERF_NODE_BINARY_PATH`) on the commands that render: Nelm `chart render`, `chart lint`, `release install`, `release plan install`; werf `converge`, `plan`, `render`, `lint`, `bundle apply`, `bundle plan`, `bundle render`. The bundle runs under `node --permission` with an empty environment, without network, process or out-of-chart file access; this guards against accidental access, not against malicious chart code.
- Charts must use `@nelm/chart-ts-sdk` 0.2.0; `nelm chart ts init` generates a `package.json`-based project.
- `helm package` (Helm's `Package` action, `werf helm package`) packs the chart as it is and no longer builds TypeScript bundles, as in upstream Helm.
Go API: `common.TypeScriptOptions`, `HelmOptions.TypeScriptOpts`, `ts.NewContextWithTSOptions`/`GetTSOptionsFromContext`, `Package.TypeScriptOps`, `ts.RunDenoInstall` and `ts.DownloadDenoForPlatform` are removed; `ts.InstallDependencies` is added; `DenoBinaryPath` is renamed to `NodeBinaryPath` in `ChartRenderOptions`, `ChartLintOptions`, `ReleaseInstallOptions`, `ReleasePlanInstallOptions` and `chart.RenderChartOptions`; `ChartTSInitOptions`, `ChartTSBuildOptions` and `ChartPackOptions` have no runtime path field.

**Migration:** Install Node.js 26 or newer wherever charts with `ts/src` are rendered or deployed (CI runners, deploy images), or pass `--node-binary-path`. A chart with `ts/src` that was deployed without `NELM_FEAT_TYPESCRIPT=true` now renders its TypeScript manifests: remove `ts/` if it was unused. Move TypeScript charts to `@nelm/chart-ts-sdk` 0.2.0 (`chart ts init` shows the new project layout: `package.json` instead of `deno.json`) and rebuild `ts/dist/bundle.js`; bundles built with SDK 0.1.x fail to render. Replace `--deno-binary-path` with `--node-binary-path` on rendering commands and drop it elsewhere; drop `NELM_FEAT_TYPESCRIPT`. Build TypeScript bundles with `nelm chart pack` or `werf bundle publish` instead of `werf helm package`.

**References:** [werf#7725](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7725), [werf#8167](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8167), [werf#8169](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8169), [nelm@cb96a15b9](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/cb96a15b9c26), [nelm@bee47f9cc](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/bee47f9ccbfb), [nelm@615df530c](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/615df530ca9d), [nelm@62d593ff8](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/62d593ff8fb4), [nelm@3abafee78](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/3abafee7837e), [nelm@4c91c3a73](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/4c91c3a739c5), [nelm@bd6de2280](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/bd6de22800ec), [nelm@0b9d576a0](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/0b9d576a0c2e), [nelm#816](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/816), [nelm#826](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/826)

#### Values schema errors are no longer turned into a warning because of service values

<a id="values-schema-validation-service-values"></a>`values-schema-validation-service-values` · change · `values` `validation` · products: nelm, werf

Before: if validating values against `values.schema.json` failed with an error containing `(root): Additional property werf is not allowed` (a schema with `additionalProperties: false` rejecting the injected `werf` service values), the whole validation result was only printed as a warning — including errors about the user's own values — and rendering continued.
Now: on a validation failure caused by service values (`werf`, `global`, ...), validation is repeated without them. If the user's values pass, rendering continues; if they still fail, rendering fails with the error about the user's values. If removing the service values changes which subcharts are enabled, rendering fails and suggests `--no-values-schema-validation`.

**Migration:** Fix values that do not match `values.schema.json`, or fix the schema. To skip the check temporarily, pass `--no-values-schema-validation` (werf: also `WERF_NO_VALUES_SCHEMA_VALIDATION=true`).

**References:** [werf#7756](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7756), [nelm@1c5d25ec2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/1c5d25ec2a27)

#### Whole-chart secret-key rotation commands are removed

<a id="cli-chart-secret-key-rotate-removed"></a>`cli-chart-secret-key-rotate-removed` · removal · `cli` `secrets` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `nelm chart secret key rotate --old-secret-key ... --new-secret-key ... [chart-dir]` re-encrypted `secret-values.yaml` and `secret/*` of a chart with a new key. In werf, `werf helm secret rotate-secret-key [EXTRA_SECRET_VALUES_FILE_PATH...]` re-encrypted `.helm/secret-values.yaml`, the `.helm/secret/` files and the given extra secret values files from the old key (`$WERF_OLD_SECRET_KEY`) to the new one (`$WERF_SECRET_KEY`).
Now: both commands are removed, and werf no longer reads `WERF_OLD_SECRET_KEY`. They missed `.werf-data/secret-values.yaml` of packed charts and subcharts (and, in Nelm, extra secret values files).

**Migration:** Re-encrypt secret files one by one, for the chart, its subcharts and any extra secret values files: decrypt each with the old key and encrypt it with the new one.
- Nelm: `nelm chart secret values-file decrypt` / `nelm chart secret file decrypt` with `--secret-key` set to the old key, then `nelm chart secret values-file encrypt` / `nelm chart secret file encrypt` with the new key.
- werf: `werf helm secret values decrypt` / `werf helm secret file decrypt` with `WERF_SECRET_KEY` set to the old key, then `werf helm secret values encrypt` / `werf helm secret file encrypt` with the new key. The werf documentation on values has a ready-made rotation script.

**References:** [werf#8142](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8142), [nelm#809](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/809)

#### `--fail-on-repo-update-fail` and `--no-update` are removed from the repository commands; `repo update` fails when any repository fails

<a id="cli-repo-update-add-flags-removed"></a>`cli-repo-update-add-flags-removed` · removal · `cli` `charts` · products: nelm, werf

Before: repository update (`nelm repo update`, `werf helm repo update`) only printed a warning when a repository index could not be downloaded and exited successfully unless `--fail-on-repo-update-fail` was passed; repository add (`nelm repo add`, `werf helm repo add`) accepted the deprecated, ignored `--no-update`.
Now: as in Helm 4, repository update always exits with an error `failed to update the following repositories: [...]` when any repository fails, and both `--fail-on-repo-update-fail` and `--no-update` are removed (passing them is an unknown-flag error).

**Migration:** Remove `--fail-on-repo-update-fail` and `--no-update` from scripts. If a failing repository must not fail the command, remove that repository or tolerate the command's exit code.

**References:** [werf@301c8f90d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/301c8f90d859), [nelm@961ca04a4](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/961ca04a485a)

#### `--values` and `--set*` override secret values, following the documented precedence

<a id="values-secret-values-precedence"></a>`values-secret-values-precedence` · change · `values` `secrets` · products: nelm, werf

Before: the chart's `secret-values.yaml` and `--secret-values` files overrode `--values` and all `--set*` options, so `--set key=null` could not delete a secret value.
Now: values are layered as documented, from lowest to highest: chart `values.yaml` < chart `secret-values.yaml` < `--values` < `--secret-values` < `--set-json` < `--set` < `--set-string` < `--set-file` < `--set-literal` < werf service values.
- `--set key=null` and `key: null` in `--values` delete keys that come from `secret-values.yaml`; `key: null` in a later `--secret-values` file deletes the key from earlier secret files.
- Subcharts: subchart `values.yaml` < subchart `secret-values.yaml` < parent `values.yaml` (`sub:` section) < parent `secret-values.yaml` (`sub:` section). A null at `sub.key` in the parent's `secret-values.yaml` no longer deletes the subchart's own `sub.key`, as with `values.yaml`.
- `--set a.b=x` fails when `--secret-values` sets `a` to a scalar, as it already did for `--values`.
- The values stored in the release now include the decrypted `--secret-values` (layered between `--values` and `--set*`), so `release get --print-values` (werf: `werf release get --print-values`) shows them, anyone who can read the release storage can read them, and a change in `--secret-values` alone creates a new revision. Releases deployed with `--secret-values` are redeployed once after the upgrade.

**Migration:** If you relied on a secret value overriding the same key from `--values` or `--set*`, remove that key from `--values`/`--set*`. Expect one redeploy of releases that use `--secret-values`, and restrict access to the release storage (Secrets, ConfigMaps or SQL) accordingly, since it now also holds the decrypted `--secret-values`.

**References:** [werf#8117](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8117), [nelm#772](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/772)

#### `.Capabilities.HelmVersion` reports Helm 4

<a id="templates-capabilities-helm-version-v4"></a>`templates-capabilities-helm-version-v4` · change · `templates` `render` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `.Capabilities.HelmVersion.Version` was `v3.14` (the Helm 3 version the embedded fork was based on).
Now: it is the Helm 4 version the embedded fork is based on (`v4.2` at the time of writing). Templates that compare `.Capabilities.HelmVersion` (e.g. `semverCompare "<4.0.0"` or `hasPrefix "v3"`) take a different branch.

**Migration:** Check templates that branch on `.Capabilities.HelmVersion` and make them accept Helm 4 versions.

**References:** [nelm@961ca04a4](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/961ca04a485a)

#### `WERF_EXPERIMENT_NO_GLOBAL_SERVICE_VALUES` is removed; `.Values.global` service values are always set

<a id="values-no-global-service-values-experiment-removed"></a>`values-no-global-service-values-experiment-removed` · removal · `values` · products: werf

Before: `WERF_EXPERIMENT_NO_GLOBAL_SERVICE_VALUES=1` stopped werf from adding its service values to `.Values.global` (such as `global.werf` and `global.env`), leaving only `.Values.werf`.
Now: the variable is ignored; werf always adds its service values under `.Values.global` (such as `global.werf`) as well as `.Values.werf`. `.Values.global.env` is no longer set, use `.Values.global.werf.env` (see `values-global-env-removed`).

**Migration:** If you set `WERF_EXPERIMENT_NO_GLOBAL_SERVICE_VALUES`, remove it, and check that charts and `values.schema.json` accept the `global.werf` service values.

**References:** [werf@2d4445b80](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/2d4445b80d9b), [werf@5bf24c417](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/5bf24c41757c)

#### `export-values` and `import-values` apply to `--values`, `--secret-values`, `--set*` and service values

<a id="values-export-import-all-layers"></a>`values-export-import-all-layers` · change · `values` `dependencies` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `export-values` and `import-values` of `Chart.yaml` dependencies were applied to the charts' `values.yaml`/`secret-values.yaml` only (plus maps from user values), so overriding a parent key with `--values`, `--set*` or werf service values (e.g. `global.werf.images.*`) did not reach the subchart, and overriding a child key did not reach the importing parent.
Now: they are applied within each values layer, from lowest to highest: `values.yaml` of all charts with `secret-values.yaml` of subcharts, the root chart's `secret-values.yaml`, `--values`, `--secret-values`, all `--set*` options together, service values. Within a layer an exported value overrides the child key and the parent's own key overrides an imported value; across layers the higher layer wins. Plain values, maps and nulls are exported; nested, multi-level and aliased dependencies are supported, also when the dependency's chart in `charts/` is out of the version range of `Chart.yaml`.
Behavior changes:
- An exported parent value overrides the child key from the same or a lower layer: `--set g.repo=a --set sub.image.repository=b` renders `a`, and service values exported to `sub.image.repository` override `--set sub.image.repository`. A `null` parent value deletes the exported child key.
- A value exported from `secret-values.yaml` overrides the child key set in the same file; a value imported from it overrides the parent key from `values.yaml`.
- Imported values follow user values: `--set sub.out.k=x` changes the parent's imported `k`.
- `--set-json` replacing an export or import source drops the copies exported or imported from lower layers; `--set list[i]=x` over an exported list patches it instead of replacing it.
- Dependency `condition:` values see plain values exported from user values; exported user values no longer appear under subcharts disabled by a condition.
- `--set sub=null` or `sub: null` for a dependency resets the subchart to its defaults instead of failing with `type mismatch on sub`.
- The values stored in the release hold `--values` < `--secret-values` < `--set*` with what `export-values` adds from them, so a release may be redeployed once after the upgrade. For charts with dependencies, the values of the chart stored in the release no longer include `--secret-values` and service values.
- Warnings: an export or import skipped because of its value (a scalar exported to a dependency root, a non-map imported) is reported as a warning, also by `chart pack` (werf: `werf bundle publish`); an `export-values` parent path or `import-values` child path set in no values (e.g. a typo) is reported as `Skipping export-values of "<path>" from chart "<chart>" to dependency "<dep>": the path is not set in any values` or `Skipping import-values of "<path>" from dependency "<dep>" to chart "<chart>": no map is set at the path in any values`. The `ImportValues missing table` warning of the Helm fork is no longer printed.
Go API: `values.Options.MergeSetValues` takes a new last argument `MergeSetValuesOptions`; `ExportUserValues` of the chart v2 util package takes one layer of values and returns the result; `ImportUserValues` is added.

**Migration:** Render your charts with the new version (`nelm chart render` / `werf render`) and compare the output if they use `export-values` or `import-values` together with `--values`, `--set*` or werf service values: a child key you set directly is now overridden by a value exported to it from the same or a higher layer. Set the parent key instead, or remove the export. Expect one redeploy of releases whose stored values change.

**References:** [werf#8117](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8117), [werf#8127](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8127), [werf#8137](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8137), [werf#8135](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8135), [nelm#773](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/773), [nelm#774](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/774), [nelm#775](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/775), [nelm#791](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/791), [nelm#806](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/806)

#### `values.schema.json` is validated with JSON Schema draft 2020-12 by default, and schemas themselves are checked

<a id="values-schema-json-schema-2020-12"></a>`values-schema-json-schema-2020-12` · change · `values` `validation` · products: nelm, werf

Before: values were validated against `values.schema.json` with the `gojsonschema` library (JSON Schema drafts 4, 6 and 7); errors looked like `- a: Invalid type. Expected: integer, given: string`.
Now: the Helm 4 validator (`santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6`) is used. A schema without `$schema` is treated as draft 2020-12 (drafts 4, 6, 7 and 2019-09 are used when `$schema` names them), the schema itself must be valid against its metaschema (otherwise rendering fails with `"file:///values.schema.json#" is not valid against metaschema`), `$ref` to `http(s)://` and `file://` URLs are resolved, and unresolved `urn:` references are ignored with a warning. Errors look like `- at '/a': got string, want integer`. A schema valid for the old validator may be rejected, or accept or reject different values, for example when it relies on draft-7-only keywords such as array-form `items`.

**Migration:** Render or lint charts with the new version. Fix schemas reported as invalid against the metaschema, or add `"$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"` to keep draft 7 semantics. Update scripts that parse schema validation error messages.

**References:** [nelm@961ca04a4](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/961ca04a485a)

#### `werf dismiss` always uninstalls releases with the Nelm uninstall implementation

<a id="cli-dismiss-native-uninstall"></a>`cli-dismiss-native-uninstall` · change · `uninstall` `cli` · products: werf

Before: `werf dismiss` uninstalled the release with the legacy Helm-based uninstall by default; the Nelm uninstall implementation was used only with `WERF_EXPERIMENT_NEW_DISMISS=1`. In the default mode `--with-hooks` (`$WERF_WITH_HOOKS`, default `true`) controlled whether hook resources from existing release revisions were deleted, and the flags `--delete-propagation`, `--save-uninstall-report`, `--uninstall-report-path` and `--uninstall-graph-path` were available only with `WERF_EXPERIMENT_NEW_DISMISS=1`.
Now: `werf dismiss` always uses the Nelm uninstall implementation (plan-based deletion with resource tracking, as `nelm release uninstall`). `WERF_EXPERIMENT_NEW_DISMISS` has no effect, `--with-hooks` and `$WERF_WITH_HOOKS` are removed, and `--delete-propagation`, `--save-uninstall-report`, `--uninstall-report-path` and `--uninstall-graph-path` are always available. `werf dismiss --use-deploy-report` reads the deploy report in the Nelm v2 format. The `Using kube context: <context>` line is no longer printed.

**Migration:** Remove `--with-hooks`, `WERF_WITH_HOOKS` and `WERF_EXPERIMENT_NEW_DISMISS` from your `werf dismiss` invocations and CI configuration. Check that the uninstall behavior (resource deletion order, tracking and hook handling) fits your release; use `--delete-propagation` and the uninstall report flags if needed.

**References:** [werf@301c8f90d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/301c8f90d859)

#### `werf helm registry login` stores OCI credentials in the Helm registry config instead of the Docker config

<a id="cli-werf-helm-registry-credentials-helm-config"></a>`cli-werf-helm-registry-credentials-helm-config` · change · `registry` `charts` `cli` · products: werf

Before: `werf helm registry login`/`logout` and the OCI operations of `werf helm` (`pull`, `dependency update`, `package` and others) stored and read registry credentials in the Docker config (`config.json` in `$WERF_DOCKER_CONFIG`, `$DOCKER_CONFIG` or `~/.docker`), so `werf helm registry login` also authenticated `werf build`, `werf converge` and other werf commands.
Now: as in Helm 4, these commands store credentials in the Helm registry config (`$HELM_REGISTRY_CONFIG`, by default `~/.config/helm/registry/config.json`) and fall back to the Docker credentials (`~/.docker/config.json` or `$DOCKER_CONFIG`) when reading. `$WERF_DOCKER_CONFIG` is ignored by `werf helm` commands. Plain-HTTP registries are enabled with `--plain-http` on the subcommands that support it.

**Migration:** Log in to registries used by werf builds and deploys with `werf cr login` or `docker login` rather than `werf helm registry login`. Set `HELM_REGISTRY_CONFIG` if you need a specific credentials file.

**References:** [werf@301c8f90d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/301c8f90d859)

#### `werf helm` no longer has get, history, list and status subcommands

<a id="cli-werf-helm-release-inspection-commands-removed"></a>`cli-werf-helm-release-inspection-commands-removed` · removal · `cli` `release-storage` · products: werf

Before: `werf helm get` with its subcommands (`all`, `hooks`, `manifest`, `notes`, `values` and others), `werf helm history`, `werf helm list` and `werf helm status` inspected releases like their Helm 3 counterparts.
Now: these subcommands are removed from `werf helm`.

**Migration:** Use `werf release list`, `werf release history` and `werf release get` (or `nelm release list`, `nelm release history`, `nelm release get`) to inspect releases: `werf release get --release NAME --namespace NAMESPACE` replaces `werf helm get` and `werf helm status`.

**References:** [werf@301c8f90d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/301c8f90d859)

#### `werf helm` no longer has install, upgrade, template, lint, uninstall, rollback and test subcommands

<a id="cli-werf-helm-deploy-commands-removed"></a>`cli-werf-helm-deploy-commands-removed` · removal · `cli` `charts` · products: werf

Before: werf embedded the Helm 3 CLI with werf chart extensions: `werf helm install`, `werf helm upgrade`, `werf helm template` and `werf helm lint` rendered charts with werf service values stubs, secret values (`--secret-values`), `--add-annotation`/`--add-label` and `--env`, and `werf helm uninstall`, `werf helm rollback` and `werf helm test` worked on releases like their Helm 3 counterparts.
Now: these subcommands are removed. `werf helm` keeps only chart, repository and registry commands (`create`, `dependency`, `env`, `package`, `pull`, `registry`, `repo`, `search`, `show`, `verify`, `version`) and the werf-specific `secret`, `get-autogenerated-values`, `get-namespace` and `get-release`.

**Migration:** Deploy and inspect charts with werf's own commands: `werf converge` instead of `werf helm install`/`upgrade`, `werf render` instead of `werf helm template`, `werf lint` instead of `werf helm lint`, `werf dismiss` instead of `werf helm uninstall`, `werf rollback` instead of `werf helm rollback`, `werf plan` to preview changes. For bundles use `werf bundle apply`/`render`/`plan`. For plain charts without a werf project use `nelm release install`, `nelm chart render`, `nelm chart lint`, `nelm release uninstall`, `nelm release rollback`, or the upstream Helm CLI. `werf helm test` has no werf replacement: run `helm test` with the upstream Helm CLI.

**References:** [werf@301c8f90d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/301c8f90d859)

#### `werf helm` no longer supports Helm plugins

<a id="cli-werf-helm-plugins-removed"></a>`cli-werf-helm-plugins-removed` · removal · `cli` · products: werf

Before: `werf helm plugin` (`install`, `list`, `uninstall`, `update`) managed Helm 3 plugins, installed plugins were loaded as `werf helm <plugin>` subcommands, and werf exited with the plugin's exit code when a plugin failed.
Now: `werf helm plugin` is removed and Helm plugins are not loaded: `werf helm <plugin>` is an unknown command.

**Migration:** Run Helm plugins with the upstream Helm CLI (`helm <plugin>`), or replace them with the corresponding werf or Nelm functionality.

**References:** [werf@301c8f90d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/301c8f90d859)

#### `werf helm` subcommands no longer accept the namespace, kube connection and progress flags

<a id="cli-werf-helm-common-flags-removed"></a>`cli-werf-helm-common-flags-removed` · removal · `cli` `logging` · products: werf

Before: every `werf helm` subcommand inherited `-n`/`--namespace` (also setting `HELM_NAMESPACE`), `--kube-config`, `--kube-config-base64`, `--kube-context`, `--status-progress-period` and `--hooks-status-progress-period` from `werf helm`, and the werf log options (`--log-debug`, `--log-verbose`, `--log-quiet`, `--log-color-mode` and others) controlled their output; `--log-debug` also enabled Helm debug output. `werf helm get-autogenerated-values` initialized a Kubernetes connection.
Now: these flags are removed from `werf helm` and its subcommands (passing them is an unknown-flag error; `werf helm get-release` keeps its own `--namespace`). The Helm-based subcommands (`create`, `dependency`, `env`, `package`, `pull`, `registry`, `repo`, `search`, `show`, `verify`, `version`) still accept the `--log-*` options but ignore them: they print uncolored output, and debug output is enabled with `HELM_DEBUG=true`. `werf helm get-autogenerated-values` no longer connects to Kubernetes.

**Migration:** Remove `-n`/`--namespace`, `--kube-config`, `--kube-config-base64`, `--kube-context`, `--status-progress-period` and `--hooks-status-progress-period` from `werf helm` invocations. Use `HELM_DEBUG=true` instead of `--log-debug` for the Helm-based subcommands.

**References:** [werf@301c8f90d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/301c8f90d859)

#### werf applies `.helmignore` when reading the chart

<a id="charts-helmignore-applied"></a>`charts-helmignore-applied` · change · `charts` `giterminism` · products: werf

Before: werf read every file of the chart directory (`.helm` by default) and ignored `.helmignore`, so files listed there still reached the rendered manifests (`werf render`, `werf converge`, `werf plan`, `werf lint`) and the bundle published by `werf bundle publish`.
Now: `.helmignore` is applied with Helm's rules, without a warning:
- files matched by `.helmignore` are excluded from rendering and from published bundles;
- Helm's default rules apply even without a `.helmignore`: dotfiles and dot-directories directly under `templates/` (e.g. `templates/.gitkeep`) are dropped;
- a leading `!` keeps only what the pattern matches and drops everything else, as in Helm;
- a `**` rule fails the command with `double-star (**) syntax is not supported`;
- a `file://` dependency is filtered by its own `.helmignore`, not by the parent's.
Excluded paths are not read and not checked by giterminism, so `.helmignore` can exclude uncommitted files. A chart with all files excluded fails with `no chart files found`. Excluded files are logged at debug level as `excluded by .helmignore`.

**Migration:** Check `.helmignore` of your charts and subcharts before upgrading: remove rules for files that must be deployed, replace `**` rules, and rename dotfiles under `templates/` that must be rendered. Compare `werf render` output (or run `werf plan`) before the first `werf converge` with werf v3.

**References:** [werf#7830](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7830), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#charts-and-bundles>

#### werf bundle copy writes OCI image layout archives and copies all platforms of images

<a id="bundle-copy-oci-layout-archive"></a>`bundle-copy-oci-layout-archive` · change · `bundles` `oci` `registry` · products: werf

Before: `werf bundle copy --to archive:PATH` wrote werf's own archive format (`chart.tar.gz` plus one `images/*.tar.gz` per image, one platform per image) and dropped the provenance file of a signed chart. Images to copy were taken from the `werf.image` values.
Now: `werf bundle copy` uses Nelm's chart copy (see `cli-chart-copy`):
- archives are written as an OCI image layout tar (`oci-layout`, `index.json`, `blobs/`); werf v2 cannot read them, werf v3 still reads archives written by werf v2;
- every image listed in `helm.sh/images` of the chart and its dependencies (and, for bundles published by werf v2, in the `werf.image` values) is copied by digest with all platforms of multi-platform images and non-distributable layers; signatures, SBOMs and other referrers are not copied;
- when copying to another repository, the image and repo values in `.werf-data/extra-values.yaml` (or `werf.image`, `werf.repo`, `global.werf.*` in `values.yaml` of werf v2 bundles) are rewritten from the copied digests;
- `--to REPO:TAG` sets the chart version from `TAG` as `werf bundle publish` does; `--to REPO` keeps the source version and tag;
- an unchanged copy keeps the chart manifest digest and its provenance; a changed copy drops the provenance with a warning;
- `--platform` and `--container-registry-mirror` are removed from `werf bundle copy`;
- `--insecure-registry` makes the chart repository plain HTTP; loopback registries are reached over plain HTTP without flags.

**Migration:** Use werf v3 on both sides of an archive transfer. Remove `--platform` and `--container-registry-mirror` from `werf bundle copy` invocations. Copy image signatures and SBOMs separately if you need them.

**References:** [werf#8143](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8143), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#charts-and-bundles>

#### werf bundle publish copies encrypted secret values into the bundle without the secret key

<a id="bundle-publish-without-secret-key"></a>`bundle-publish-without-secret-key` · change · `bundles` `secrets` · products: werf

Before: `werf bundle publish` decrypted the secret values (`.helm/secret-values.yaml` and `--secret-values` files) with the secret key and re-encrypted them into the bundle. Without `WERF_SECRET_KEY` (or `.werf_secret_key`), it only logged `Secrets decryption disabled due to missed key` and published the bundle without any secret values. It accepted `--secret-key` (`$WERF_SECRET_KEY`) and `--ignore-secret-key` (`$WERF_IGNORE_SECRET_KEY`).
Now: `werf bundle publish` does not need the secret key: the encrypted secret values files are merged as they are and always stored in the bundle. `--secret-key` and `--ignore-secret-key` are removed from `werf bundle publish`. The key is still needed by `werf bundle apply`, `werf bundle plan` and `werf bundle render` to decrypt the values.

**Migration:** Remove `--secret-key` and `--ignore-secret-key` from `werf bundle publish` invocations. Bundles published without the key now contain the secret values, so the commands that deploy them need the secret key the values were encrypted with.

**References:** [werf#7525](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7525), [werf#7542](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7542)

#### werf bundle publish no longer stores the `werf.io/release-channel` annotation in the bundle

<a id="bundle-publish-release-channel-dropped"></a>`bundle-publish-release-channel-dropped` · change · `bundles` `annotations` · products: werf

Before: `werf bundle publish` saved the `werf.io/release-channel` annotation of the publishing werf (from `--add-annotation werf.io/release-channel=...`, which `werf ci-env` exports as `WERF_ADD_ANNOTATION_WERF_RELEASE_CHANNEL` from `TRDL_USE_WERF_GROUP_CHANNEL`) into the bundle's extra annotations, and every resource deployed from the bundle got it.
Now: `werf bundle publish` drops `werf.io/release-channel` silently. Resources deployed with `werf bundle apply` get the annotation only if the applying werf is given one (`--add-annotation` or `WERF_ADD_ANNOTATION_*`, e.g. from `werf ci-env`). Bundles published by earlier werf versions still carry the stored channel. Other annotations are unaffected.

**Migration:** If you select or report on `werf.io/release-channel` of bundle-deployed resources, pass `--add-annotation werf.io/release-channel=<channel>` to `werf bundle apply` (or run it after `werf ci-env`).

**References:** [werf#7831](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7831)

#### werf converge and werf plan accept image names as arguments without `WERF_CONVERGE_ENABLE_IMAGES_PARAMS`

<a id="converge-plan-image-name-args"></a>`converge-plan-image-name-args` · change · `cli` `images` · products: werf

Before: `werf converge [IMAGE_NAME ...]` and `werf plan [IMAGE_NAME ...]` limited the processed images to the given names only with `WERF_CONVERGE_ENABLE_IMAGES_PARAMS=1`; otherwise positional arguments were silently ignored and all images were processed.
Now: positional arguments always select the images to process, as in `werf build` (names and glob patterns, `!pattern` excludes); the environment variable is no longer read. A name that matches no image in `werf.yaml` is an error.

**Migration:** Remove positional arguments from `werf converge` and `werf plan` calls that passed them by mistake, otherwise only the listed images are built and passed to the chart. Drop `WERF_CONVERGE_ENABLE_IMAGES_PARAMS` from the environment.

**References:** [werf#7616](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7616)

#### werf deploys with Nelm v2, and `werf helm` uses the Nelm v2 Helm 4 fork

<a id="deploy-nelm-v2-engine"></a>`deploy-nelm-v2-engine` · change · `charts` `dependencies` · products: werf

Before: werf v2 used Nelm v1 (with its Helm 3-based fork) for `werf converge`, `werf plan`, `werf render`, `werf lint`, `werf rollback`, `werf dismiss` and the `werf bundle` commands, and a separate legacy Helm 3 stack (`3p-helm-for-werf-helm`, `nelm-for-werf-helm`, `kubedog-for-werf-helm`) for the `werf helm` subcommands.
Now: all of them use Nelm v2 and its Helm 4-based fork; the legacy Helm 3 stack is removed. Every Nelm v2 change marked for werf in this catalogue (chart loading, values, templates, rendering, plan, apply, tracking, release storage, secrets, reports) applies to werf v3.

**Migration:** Review the deploy changes of this catalogue that list werf among their products, render your charts with werf v3 (`werf render`) and compare the result, and check the plan (`werf plan`) before the first deploy with werf v3.

**References:** [werf@301c8f90d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/301c8f90d859)

#### werf no longer reads the release storage driver from `HELM_DRIVER`

<a id="release-storage-werf-helm-driver-env-ignored"></a>`release-storage-werf-helm-driver-env-ignored` · removal · `release-storage` `cli` · products: werf

Before: when `$WERF_RELEASE_STORAGE` was not set, the default of `--release-storage` was taken from `$HELM_DRIVER` (for example `HELM_DRIVER=configmap` made werf store releases in ConfigMaps).
Now: only `--release-storage` and `$WERF_RELEASE_STORAGE` are read; `$HELM_DRIVER` is ignored and releases are stored in Secrets unless configured otherwise.

**Migration:** If you relied on `HELM_DRIVER`, set `WERF_RELEASE_STORAGE` to the same value (or pass `--release-storage`), otherwise werf will not find releases stored in ConfigMaps or SQL and will create new ones in Secrets.

**References:** [werf#7518](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7518)

#### werf no longer sets `.Values.global.env`; use `.Values.werf.env` or `.Values.global.werf.env`

<a id="values-global-env-removed"></a>`values-global-env-removed` · removal · `values` · products: werf

Before: werf set the service value `.Values.global.env` to the `--env` value (an empty string with stub values in `werf render`) in `werf converge`, `werf plan`, `werf render`, `werf lint` and the `werf bundle` deploy commands, in addition to `.Values.werf.env`.
Now: `.Values.global.env` is not set: templates that read it get an empty value without an error. The environment remains available as `.Values.werf.env` in the main chart and `.Values.global.werf.env` in the main chart and dependencies. For temporary compatibility `WERF_LEGACY_VALUES_GLOBAL_ENV=1` restores `.Values.global.env`.

**Migration:** Replace `.Values.global.env` with `.Values.global.werf.env` (or `.Values.werf.env` in the main chart) in templates and `values.schema.json`. Set `WERF_LEGACY_VALUES_GLOBAL_ENV=1` only as a temporary workaround.

**References:** [werf#7636](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7636), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#values-and-environment-variables>

### Cleanup

#### Host cleanup removes stale host lock files

<a id="host-cleanup-stale-lock-files"></a>`host-cleanup-stale-lock-files` · fix · `host-cleanup` · products: werf

Before: lock files under `~/.werf/service/locks/` (`$WERF_HOME/service/locks/`) were never removed after a lock was released, so on long-lived runners they accumulated into millions of empty files and could exhaust inodes; because they are empty, they never triggered automatic host cleanup.
Now: `werf host cleanup`, including the automatic one, removes lock files that are not held by any process and are older than 24 hours, and 10000 or more such files trigger automatic host cleanup on their own. Acquiring a lock detects a lock file removed concurrently and retries.
Older werf v2 binaries do not have this retry: when v2 and v3 run concurrently with the same `$WERF_HOME`, the v3 cleanup can remove a lock file that a v2 process has just opened, so both may hold the same lock. Separate `$WERF_HOME` directories do not help: the container backend has one image store per host, so a v3 host cleanup does not see image locks of a running v2 build and can delete its stage images.

**Migration:** Do not run werf v2 and werf v3 concurrently on the same runner or with the same container backend storage. Drain v2 jobs on a runner before switching it to v3, or migrate on separate runners or backend stores.

**References:** [werf#7619](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7619), [werf#7700](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7700), [lockgate@8d77d5d1e](https://github.com/werf/lockgate/commit/8d77d5d1eea0), <https://github.com/werf/werf/issues/6127>

#### Registry API credential flags (`--repo-docker-hub-token`, `--repo-github-token`, ...) are accepted only by commands that delete registry data

<a id="cleanup-registry-api-credential-flags-only-for-deletion"></a>`cleanup-registry-api-credential-flags-only-for-deletion` · removal · `cli` `registry` · products: werf

Before: every command working with `--repo`/`--final-repo` accepted the registry API credentials used only for deleting tags: `--repo-docker-hub-username`, `--repo-docker-hub-password`, `--repo-docker-hub-token`, `--repo-github-token`, `--repo-harbor-username`, `--repo-harbor-password`, `--repo-quay-token` and the same `--final-repo-*` flags, with their `WERF_REPO_*`/`WERF_FINAL_REPO_*` environment variables (e.g. `werf build`, `converge`, `plan`, `render`, `run`, `export`, `bundle publish`, `managed-images ls`).
Now: only `werf cleanup` and `werf purge` accept both groups, and `werf managed-images rm` and `werf meta-repo detach` accept the `--repo-*` group. Other commands reject these flags and ignore the environment variables. Registry authentication for pulling and pushing (Docker config, `werf cr login`) is unchanged.

**Migration:** Remove `--repo-docker-hub-*`, `--repo-github-token`, `--repo-harbor-*`, `--repo-quay-token` and their `--final-repo-*` counterparts from invocations of commands other than `cleanup`, `purge`, `managed-images rm` and `meta-repo detach`; passing them is now an unknown-flag error. Environment variables can stay.

**References:** [werf#8086](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8086)

## Deprecations

### Build

#### `imageSpec.config.clearWerfLabels` is deprecated

<a id="build-clear-werf-labels-deprecated"></a>`build-clear-werf-labels-deprecated` · deprecation · `config` `images` · products: werf

Before: `imageSpec.config.clearWerfLabels` (and `build.imageSpec.config.clearWerfLabels` in the meta section) was accepted silently, although it never had any effect on built images.
Now: it still has no effect, and werf prints a deprecation warning when it is set to `true`.

**Migration:** Remove `clearWerfLabels` from `werf.yaml`. To drop werf labels, use `imageSpec.config.removeLabels` (essential werf labels are kept) or `werf export`, which removes all werf labels by default.

**References:** [werf#7629](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7629)

## New features

### General

#### JSON Schemas for `werf.yaml`, `werf-giterminism.yaml` and `werf-includes.yaml` are published for editors

<a id="config-json-schemas-published"></a>`config-json-schemas-published` · feature · `config` · products: werf

New: werf publishes JSON Schemas for its configuration files at `https://werf.io/docs/v3/schemas/werf.json`, `werf-giterminism.json` and `werf-includes.json`. Attached to an editor with a YAML language server (VS Code with Red Hat YAML, JetBrains IDEs, Neovim), e.g. with a `# yaml-language-server: $schema=...` comment, they provide completion, hover documentation and validation: unknown keys and mutually exclusive directives are reported, and deprecated directives (`fromImage`, `image` in `import`/`dependencies`, ...) are struck through. The schemas only help editing; werf's own validation of these files is unchanged.

**References:** [werf#7860](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7860)

#### `werf kube-run` accepts the full set of Kubernetes connection flags

<a id="kube-run-full-kube-connection-flags"></a>`kube-run-full-kube-connection-flags` · feature · `kube-run` · products: werf

Before: `werf kube-run` accepted only `--kube-config`, `--kube-config-base64` and `--kube-context` and connected to the cluster with the kubedog client.
Now: `werf kube-run` connects through the Nelm Kubernetes client and accepts the same connection flags as `werf converge`: `--kube-api-server`, `--kube-token`, `--kube-token-path`, `--kube-ca-path`, `--kube-ca-data`, `--kube-cert`, `--kube-cert-data`, `--kube-key`, `--kube-key-data`, `--kube-tls-server`, `--skip-tls-verify-kube`, `--kube-auth-username`, `--kube-auth-password`, `--kube-auth-provider`, `--kube-auth-provider-config`, `--kube-context-cluster`, `--kube-context-user`, `--kube-impersonate-user`, `--kube-impersonate-group`, `--kube-impersonate-uid`, `--kube-proxy-url`, `--kube-request-timeout`, `--kube-qps-limit` and `--kube-burst-limit` (with the corresponding `WERF_*` environment variables).

**References:** [werf@301c8f90d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/301c8f90d859)

#### werf images get `-node` variants with Node.js for TypeScript charts

<a id="distribution-werf-node-images"></a>`distribution-werf-node-images` · feature · `distribution` `typescript` · products: werf

Before: werf images (`registry.werf.io/werf/werf`, `ghcr.io/werf/werf`) and the Argo CD sidecar image had no JavaScript runtime.
Now: `ubuntu-node`, `centos-node` and `fedora-node` variants of the werf images, and `ubuntu-node` of `werf-argocd-cmp-sidecar`, carry Node.js 26, npm, pnpm and yarn, so TypeScript charts can be rendered in CI from a werf image. Tags: `<group>-<channel>-<os>-node`, `<version>-<os>-node`, `<group>-<os>-node`; there is no `alpine` `-node` variant and no `-node` tag without the OS. They are published for werf 3.13.0 and newer; existing tags don't change.

**References:** [werf#8168](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8168), <https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8168>

### Build

#### Operations reporting covers content digests and the local image list cache

<a id="build-report-content-and-local-cache-observations"></a>`build-report-content-and-local-cache-observations` · feature · `build-report` `cache` · products: werf

New: with operations reporting enabled (`--build-report-operations`, or debug logging), the operations summary and the saved build report also include `build: content digests` and `build: content cache resolve` (calculating content-based tags and looking images up by them), and the cache summary also counts lookups in the in-memory cache of the local Docker or Buildah image list (`docker: image list`, `buildah: image list`): hits, misses, bypasses and requests shared with a concurrent listing. The rest of the operations report, including the Git preparation operations, is already in werf v2.

**References:** [werf#8002](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8002), [werf#8003](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8003), [werf#8068](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8068)

#### The stapel image is embedded in the werf binary and needs no registry access

<a id="build-stapel-image-embedded"></a>`build-stapel-image-embedded` · feature · `stapel` `distribution` · products: werf

Before: on first use, werf pulled the stapel image `registry.werf.io/werf/stapel` from the registry; air-gapped setups had to mirror it and set `WERF_STAPEL_IMAGE_NAME`/`WERF_STAPEL_IMAGE_VERSION`.
Now: release binaries embed the stapel image for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`, and werf loads it with `docker load` instead of pulling it, unless `WERF_STAPEL_IMAGE_NAME` or `WERF_STAPEL_IMAGE_VERSION` is set. Other platforms and custom images are still pulled. Release binaries are about 35–40 MB larger.

**References:** [werf#7601](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7601), [werf@5fe36bc78](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/5fe36bc78eca)

#### `dockerfile:` may point outside `context:` within the project directory

<a id="build-dockerfile-outside-context"></a>`build-dockerfile-outside-context` · feature · `dockerfile` `config` · products: werf

Before: `dockerfile:` had to be inside `context:`; for example, `context: app` with `dockerfile: ../build/app.Dockerfile` failed with `'dockerfile: PATH' required and should be relative to context!`.
Now: `dockerfile:` may leave the context via `..` as long as the resulting path stays inside the project directory; absolute paths are still rejected. Such a Dockerfile is not added to the build context. The file must be committed like any other Dockerfile (giterminism).

**References:** [werf#7722](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7722)

#### `werf build` publishes final images to several final repositories

<a id="build-multiple-final-repos"></a>`build-multiple-final-repos` · feature · `registry` `cli` · products: werf

Before: `--final-repo` accepted one repository.
Now: `werf build` accepts `--final-repo` several times, or `WERF_FINAL_REPO` together with numbered `WERF_FINAL_REPO_1`, `WERF_FINAL_REPO_2`, ... variables; final images (complete multi-platform indexes included) and custom tags are published to every destination, sharing `--parallel-tasks-limit`. CLI flags replace the environment values, duplicates are processed once, and the build report refers to the first final repository. Other commands keep a single final repository.

**References:** [werf#8087](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8087)

### Deploy

#### A JSON Schema for `Chart.yaml` with the werf `export-values` extension is published for editors

<a id="charts-chart-yaml-json-schema"></a>`charts-chart-yaml-json-schema` · feature · `charts` `dependencies` · products: werf

New: werf publishes a `Chart.yaml` schema at `https://werf.io/docs/v3/schemas/chart.json`, next to the `werf.yaml` schemas. Unlike the standard Helm schema from JSON Schema Store, which reports `export-values` in `dependencies` as `Additional properties are not allowed`, it accepts `export-values` (a string path or a `parent`/`child` object; an empty or `.` `parent` is rejected) and allows `apiVersion`, `name` and `version` to be omitted in the main chart, since werf fills them in. Unknown keys are still rejected. The schema is not registered in JSON Schema Store: select it explicitly, e.g. with a `# yaml-language-server: $schema=...` comment. werf's own chart handling is unchanged.

**References:** [werf#8153](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8153)

#### A warning is printed when a resource being deployed is already being deleted

<a id="deploy-warn-terminating-resource"></a>`deploy-warn-terminating-resource` · feature · `resources` `logging` · products: nelm, werf

New: install, plan install, rollback and auto-rollback print a warning when the live object of a resource being deployed has `metadata.deletionTimestamp` set (Terminating, e.g. held by a finalizer), saying that it is being deleted and won't be recreated by this deploy; for PersistentVolumeClaims and PersistentVolumes it adds that Pods using it will fail to schedule once recreated and its data may be lost. Before, such an object was silently updated or left as is and could be reported ready. Resources planned for recreation don't get the warning. The plan, tracking and exit code are unchanged.

**References:** [werf#8124](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8124), [nelm#790](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/790)

#### A warning lists secret values in the old format that are read as strings

<a id="secrets-warn-legacy-untyped-values"></a>`secrets-warn-legacy-untyped-values` · feature · `secrets` `values` · products: nelm, werf

Values encrypted in the old format do not store their YAML type and are read as strings, which can make `values.schema.json` checks for `integer`, `boolean` or `number` fail with no hint why.
Now, when a secret values file (including `.werf-data/secret-values.yaml` of a published chart) contains old-format values that would be numbers or booleans as plain YAML, a warning is printed once per file, listing their paths and suggesting to re-enter them with the secret values edit command.

**References:** [werf#8122](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8122), [nelm#796](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/796), [common-go#38](https://github.com/werf/common-go/pull/38)

#### Charts with `apiVersion: v3` are supported

<a id="chart-api-version-v3"></a>`chart-api-version-v3` · feature · `charts` · products: nelm, werf

New: charts with `apiVersion: v3` in `Chart.yaml` (the Helm 4 chart format) can be rendered, linted, packed and deployed, with releases stored in a format Helm reads. For v3 charts:
- subcharts get their own `secret-values.yaml` applied, declared in `dependencies` or not, aliased or not;
- `import-values` apply to every values layer: values.yaml < chart `secret-values.yaml` < `--values` < `--secret-values` < `--set*` < service values;
- `export-values` are not supported: they are ignored with a warning `Ignoring export-values of dependency "<dep>" of chart "<chart>": export-values are not supported in charts with apiVersion v3`.
Release info annotations (`--release-info-annotations`) are stored for v3 charts like for v2 charts.

**References:** [werf#8028](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8028), [werf#8133](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8133), [werf#8129](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8129), [nelm@961ca04a4](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/961ca04a485a), [nelm@ae98e045c](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/ae98e045c538), [nelm@8f935db93](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8f935db93024), [nelm#742](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/742), [nelm#803](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/803), [nelm#795](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/795)

#### Group, version and kind in deploy and delete dependency annotations are matched case-insensitively

<a id="dependency-annotations-gvk-case-insensitive"></a>`dependency-annotations-gvk-case-insensitive` · feature · `annotations` `tracking` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `group`, `version` and `kind` in `werf.io/deploy-dependency-<id>` and `werf.io/delete-dependency-<id>` had to be spelled exactly as in the resource, e.g. `kind=StatefulSet`; `kind=statefulset` did not match the dependency or the cluster resource.
Now: they are compared case-insensitively, both when matching resources of the release and when tracking presence, readiness or absence of external resources, so `kind=statefulset` and `kind=StatefulSet` are equivalent.

**References:** [nelm#626](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/626), [kubedog#394](https://github.com/werf/kubedog/pull/394)

#### Helm-based chart and repository commands get the Helm 4 flags

<a id="cli-chart-commands-helm-4-flags"></a>`cli-chart-commands-helm-4-flags` · feature · `cli` `charts` · products: nelm, werf

The commands built on Helm follow Helm 4 and get new flags.
Nelm (`nelm chart dependency download|update`, `nelm chart download` and the `nelm chart repo` commands):
- all of them: `--color`/`--colour` (`never`, `auto`, `always`) and `--content-cache` (default `~/.cache/helm/content`, a content-addressed cache of downloaded charts);
- `nelm chart dependency download|update`: `--username`, `--password`, `--ca-file`, `--cert-file`, `--key-file`, `--insecure-skip-tls-verify` and `--plain-http` for accessing the chart repository;
- `nelm chart repo login`: `--plain-http`;
- `nelm chart repo add` and `nelm chart repo update`: `--timeout` (default `2m0s`) for downloading the index file.
werf (`werf helm` subcommands; they do not get `--color`/`--colour` or `--content-cache`):
- `werf helm dependency build`, `werf helm dependency update` and `werf helm package`: `--username`, `--password`, `--ca-file`, `--cert-file`, `--key-file`, `--insecure-skip-tls-verify` and `--plain-http` for accessing the chart repository;
- `werf helm registry login`: `--plain-http`;
- `werf helm repo add` and `werf helm repo update`: `--timeout` (default `2m0s`);
- `werf helm repo list`: `--no-headers`.

**References:** [werf@301c8f90d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/301c8f90d859), [nelm@961ca04a4](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/961ca04a485a)

#### Templates can use the Helm 4 functions `fromToml`, `mustToToml`, `mustToYaml` and `toYamlPretty`

<a id="templates-helm-4-functions"></a>`templates-helm-4-functions` · feature · `templates` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `fromToml`, `mustToToml`, `mustToYaml` and `toYamlPretty` were not defined; using them failed rendering with `function "fromToml" not defined`.
Now: chart templates can use them, as in Helm 4: `fromToml` parses a TOML string into a map, `mustToToml` and `mustToYaml` are like `toToml` and `toYaml` but fail rendering on a serialization error instead of returning an empty string or an error message, and `toYamlPretty` renders YAML with 2-space indentation, lists included.

**References:** [nelm@961ca04a4](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/961ca04a485a)

#### `--no-values-schema-validation` disables validation of values against `values.schema.json`

<a id="values-schema-validation-disable-option"></a>`values-schema-validation-disable-option` · feature · `values` `validation` `cli` · products: nelm, werf

Before: values were always validated against the chart's `values.schema.json`; there was no way to skip it.
Now: `--no-values-schema-validation` (`$NELM_NO_VALUES_SCHEMA_VALIDATION`; werf: `$WERF_NO_VALUES_SCHEMA_VALIDATION`) skips this validation in `nelm chart render`, `nelm chart lint`, `nelm release install`, `nelm release plan install`, `nelm release rollback` and the corresponding werf deploy, render and lint commands. The Go API has `NoValuesSchemaValidation` in the action options.

**References:** [werf#7756](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7756), [nelm#616](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/616)

#### `werf.io/triggers-release: "false"` keeps a resource from causing a new release on its own

<a id="annotations-triggers-release"></a>`annotations-triggers-release` · feature · `annotations` `plan` · products: nelm, werf

New: the `werf.io/triggers-release: "true"|"false"` resource annotation (default `"true"`). With `"false"`, when deciding whether the release is up to date and the deploy can be skipped, Nelm ignores changes in the resource's manifest and all operations on it: creation, update, recreation (e.g. caused by `werf.io/delete-policy: before-creation` or the default delete policy of hooks), deletion and readiness tracking. Useful for Jobs that should run only when something else is deployed (migrations, backups, notifications): without it, a Job with `werf.io/delete-policy: before-creation` is recreated on every deploy, so the release is never skipped.
Adding such a resource to the chart, removing it, or its absence in the cluster (e.g. deleted by `werf.io/delete-policy: succeeded` or `ttlSecondsAfterFinished`) doesn't trigger a release either; it is created or deleted with the next release. Values are always compared as a whole, so changing values used only by such a resource still triggers a release.

**References:** [nelm#779](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/779)

#### werf bundle plan saves and shows plan artifacts, werf bundle apply deploys them with `--use-plan`

<a id="bundle-plan-artifacts"></a>`bundle-plan-artifacts` · feature · `bundles` `plan` · products: werf

Before: saving a plan and deploying exactly that plan was available only for `werf plan --save-plan` and `werf converge --use-plan`.
Now: the bundle commands support it too. `werf bundle plan --save-plan PATH` (`$WERF_SAVE_PLAN_PATH`) saves the gzip-compressed JSON install plan, `werf bundle plan --show-plan PATH` (`$WERF_SHOW_PLAN_PATH`) prints the changes of a saved plan, and `werf bundle apply --use-plan PATH` (`$WERF_USE_PLAN_PATH`) deploys the saved plan; `--plan-lifetime` (`$WERF_PLAN_LIFETIME`, default `2h`) limits how old the plan may be.

**References:** [werf#7543](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7543)

#### werf release get, list and history inspect deployed releases

<a id="cli-werf-release-commands"></a>`cli-werf-release-commands` · feature · `cli` `release-storage` · products: werf

New commands to inspect releases, backed by the Nelm `release get`, `release list` and `release history` actions:
- `werf release list [--namespace NS]` lists releases; `--output-format table|yaml|json` (default `table`).
- `werf release history --release NAME --namespace NS` shows the revisions of a release; `--revisions-limit N` (`$WERF_RELEASE_HISTORY_REVISIONS_LIMIT`, default `0`, no limit) and `--output-format table|yaml|json` (default `table`).
- `werf release get [REVISION] --release NAME --namespace NS` prints a release revision (the latest by default) with its chart, resources and labels; `--print-values` adds the computed values; `--output-format yaml|json` (default `yaml`).
All three accept the kube connection flags, `--release-storage` and `--release-storage-sql-connection`; `--output-format` also reads `$WERF_OUTPUT_FORMAT`. They do not read `werf.yaml`, so `--release` (`$WERF_RELEASE`) and `--namespace` (`$WERF_NAMESPACE`) have to be passed explicitly. With the default log settings their JSON/YAML output is machine-readable: no informational lines before the document and no ANSI colors added because of GitHub Actions or GitLab CI detection.

**References:** [werf@08a54a33f](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/08a54a33f238), [werf@9a8030a32](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/9a8030a329a9), [werf@44572711c](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/44572711c987), [werf@018f103f5](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/018f103f5ff5), [werf@76a3c5184](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/76a3c5184319), [werf#7961](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7961), [werf#8083](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8083)

### Cleanup

#### `werf cleanup --keep-list` accepts custom tags

<a id="cleanup-keep-list-custom-tags"></a>`cleanup-keep-list-custom-tags` · feature · `cleanup` · products: werf

Before: `--keep-list` lines were matched only against stage tags (`DIGEST-TIMESTAMP`); a custom tag added with `--add-custom-tag` (e.g. `main`, `pr42`) in the list protected nothing.
Now: a line equal to a custom tag protects the stage the tag points to (reason `keep list` in the cleanup report) and the custom tag itself. A custom tag whose stage no longer exists protects nothing. Stage-tag lines behave as before.

**References:** [werf#8139](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8139)

#### werf reports the result of the last automatic host cleanup on the next run

<a id="host-cleanup-auto-cleanup-notice"></a>`host-cleanup-auto-cleanup-notice` · feature · `host-cleanup` `logging` · products: werf

Before: automatic host cleanup ran in the background and wrote its output only to a service log, so images it removed and the rebuilds that followed were unexplained.
Now: when a background host cleanup frees space, the next suitable werf command prints once how long ago it ran, how many local images werf removed and how much space was freed in total, with the storage usage and the allowed limit. If usage is still above the allowed level (`--allowed-backend-storage-volume-usage` and related options), the message is a warning with ways to fix it. Commands with machine-readable output keep the notice for a later command (unless verbose or debug output is requested). Manual `werf host cleanup` and dry runs do not produce a notice.

**References:** [werf@81cf86ff6](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/81cf86ff6a2d)

## Other changes

### General

#### Published Linux and Windows binaries of Nelm and werf are compressed with upx

<a id="distribution-upx-compressed-binaries"></a>`distribution-upx-compressed-binaries` · change · `distribution` · products: nelm, werf

Before: Nelm and werf release binaries were published uncompressed (Nelm linux/amd64 about 120 MB).
Now: the published Linux and Windows binaries are compressed with upx and unpack themselves in memory on start, so they are much smaller to download: Nelm linux/amd64 is about 70 MB; werf `linux-amd64`, `linux-arm64` and `windows-amd64` binaries distributed via trdl are compressed with `upx --best`. macOS binaries are not compressed.
Some antivirus, EDR or binary-scanning tools flag UPX-packed executables, and tools that inspect the binary (e.g. `go version -m`) cannot read the packed file.

**References:** [werf#7652](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7652), [werf#7744](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7744), [werf#7753](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7753), [nelm#731](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/731)

#### `LOCKGATE_DEBUG=1` diagnostics of distributed locks go to stderr

<a id="logging-lockgate-debug-stderr"></a>`logging-lockgate-debug-stderr` · change · `logging` `locking` · products: werf

Before: with the undocumented `LOCKGATE_DEBUG=1`, the debug messages of the lockgate distributed locker (used by `werf synchronization` and with an HTTP `--synchronization` server) were printed to stdout, mixed into the command output.
Now: they are printed to stderr.

**References:** [lockgate@1acbd7fb8](https://github.com/werf/lockgate/commit/1acbd7fb84f2)

#### `werf-includes.lock` is written with two-space indentation

<a id="giterminism-includes-lock-two-space-indent"></a>`giterminism-includes-lock-two-space-indent` · change · `giterminism` · products: werf

Before: `werf includes update` wrote `werf-includes.lock` with four-space YAML indentation.
Now: the file is written with two-space indentation. The content is the same; regenerating the lock file produces a whitespace-only diff once.

**References:** [werf#7840](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7840)

#### werf no longer checks for an outdated multiwerf

<a id="cli-multiwerf-warning-removed"></a>`cli-multiwerf-warning-removed` · change · `cli` `distribution` · products: werf

Before: `werf build`, `converge`, `plan`, `lint`, `render`, `run`, `kube-run`, `rollback` and the `bundle` commands ran `multiwerf version` when `multiwerf` was in `PATH` and printed a warning recommending to switch to trdl if it was older than 1.5.0 or its version could not be detected.
