Now: werf does not look for multiwerf and prints no such warning. multiwerf is not supported; install werf with trdl.

**References:** [werf@d054d24f9](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/d054d24f9e6e)

### Build

#### Build output, especially debug output, is less repetitive

<a id="build-less-repetitive-output"></a>`build-less-repetitive-output` · change · `logging` · products: werf

Before: builds printed the `Using git stages` detail line for every image, per-task worker-start messages, stage-digest lock progress on every lock, repeated repository/commit lines, and full `git show-ref`/`git ls-remote` output in debug logs.
Now: these lines are removed or printed once (lock progress only when the lock is contended); the full Git ref listing is printed only with `WERF_DEBUG_TRUE_GIT=1`.

**References:** [werf#7985](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7985)

#### Cached Git stages are reused without requiring their commit to be an ancestor of the current commit

<a id="build-git-ancestry-check-removed"></a>`build-git-ancestry-check-removed` · change · `git` `cache` `stapel` · products: werf

Before: werf reused a cached `gitArchive`, `gitCache` or `gitLatestPatch` stage only if the commit recorded on it was a Git ancestor of the current commit; after `git commit --amend`, a rebase or a branch switch, such stages were rebuilt, together with every dependent image. `WERF_DISABLE_GIT_COMMIT_ANCESTRY_CHECK=1` turned the check off.
Now: the ancestry check is removed; a cached Git stage only requires its recorded commit to still exist in the repository. `WERF_DISABLE_GIT_COMMIT_ANCESTRY_CHECK` no longer has any effect.

**Migration:** Remove `WERF_DISABLE_GIT_COMMIT_ANCESTRY_CHECK` from CI settings; it is no longer needed.

**References:** [werf#7615](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7615), [werf#7746](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7746)

#### Image config changes of `imageSpec` are committed natively instead of saving and reloading the image

<a id="build-native-image-config-mutation"></a>`build-native-image-config-mutation` · change · `images` `performance` · products: werf

Before: to change the config of a built image (the `imageSpec` stage and the content-based tag), werf saved the image to a tar archive, edited its config and loaded it back into the Docker daemon or Buildah storage.
Now: with the Buildah backend and the Docker server backend, werf creates a container from the image, applies the config and commits it, without the save/load round trip of the whole image. The Docker backend takes this path only when the change is purely additive (no cleared fields, no removed labels, environment variables, volumes or exposed ports) and otherwise falls back to save/load; an image committed by Docker gets an additional history entry.

**References:** [werf#7634](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7634)

#### Images are identified by a content-based tag and reused as a whole when their content inputs are unchanged

<a id="build-content-based-tag"></a>`build-content-based-tag` · change · `images` `cache` `performance` · products: werf

Before: the image tag was the tag of the last non-empty stage (`DIGEST-TIMESTAMP_MILLISEC`), and every build walked through all stages of every image, checking each stage in the stages storage.
Now: the last stage of each image is a content anchor whose digest is calculated up front from the target platform and all inputs of the image: instructions and stage digests, Git content (including file modes), build context, base images, dependencies and the cache version. The image is published with this content-based tag. When an image with the same content-based tag already exists in the stages storage (or can be copied from a secondary storage), werf reuses it without processing its stages and logs `Use previously built image for <image> by content-based tag`; a stored anchor is reused even if the Git commit it was built from is no longer available. Non-final images that no image being built needs are skipped.

**References:** [werf@55dc5ea4b](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/55dc5ea4b013), [werf@7f71de96b](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/7f71de96b373), [werf@c27d5c81d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/c27d5c81d45b), [werf@9d307eec6](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/9d307eec6232), [werf@cbd8e77dc](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/cbd8e77dc193), [werf#7638](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7638), [werf#7764](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7764), [werf#7827](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7827), [werf#7838](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7838), [werf#7874](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7874), [werf#7876](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7876), [werf#7882](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7882), [werf#7894](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7894), [werf@1ba2e9ff0](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/1ba2e9ff02be), [werf#7931](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7931), [werf#7940](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7940), [werf#7947](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7947), [werf#7959](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7959), [werf@1191bf126](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/1191bf1264fb), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#building>

#### Images start building as soon as their own dependencies are built

<a id="build-parallel-image-scheduling"></a>`build-parallel-image-scheduling` · change · `performance` `images` `logging` · products: werf

Before: parallel builds grouped images into dependency levels ("waves") and built one level at a time, so an image waited for every image of the previous level, even unrelated slow ones.
Now: images are scheduled by the real dependency graph (`from`, `import`, `dependencies`, and `FROM`/`COPY --from`/`RUN --mount=from` in staged Dockerfiles): an image starts as soon as the images it depends on are done, limited by `--parallel-tasks-limit`. The log of the oldest still-running image is streamed live and the other images follow in start order; each image's output stays one uninterrupted block. The `(N/Total)` progress number of image blocks and of `Build summary` reflects the order in which images actually start, and the "Concurrent build plan" listing shows images without it.

**References:** [werf#7688](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7688), [werf#7703](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7703), [werf#7863](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7863)

#### Stapel uses a new multi-platform stapel image and builds linux/arm64 on the Docker backend by default

<a id="build-stapel-multiplatform-image"></a>`build-stapel-multiplatform-image` · change · `stapel` `platform` · products: werf

Before: Stapel used the `registry.werf.io/werf/stapel:0.6.2` image (glibc toolchain, linux/amd64 only). With the Docker server backend, Stapel images could be built only for `linux/amd64`; `linux/arm64` required `WERF_EXPERIMENTAL_STAPEL_ARM=1`.
Now: the stapel image is rebuilt as a multi-platform image (`registry.werf.io/werf/stapel:0.7.x`, `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`), and werf pulls the variant matching the build platform. Stapel images on the Docker server backend build for `linux/arm64` (and its variants) out of the box; `WERF_EXPERIMENTAL_STAPEL_ARM` is no longer needed. Platforms other than `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` are still unsupported with the Docker server backend.

**Migration:** If you mirror the stapel image and point werf to it with `WERF_STAPEL_IMAGE_NAME`/`WERF_STAPEL_IMAGE_VERSION`, mirror the new version used by werf v3 with all its platforms. Remove `WERF_EXPERIMENTAL_STAPEL_ARM` from the environment.

**References:** [werf#7403](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7403), [werf@6a20bf23d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/6a20bf23db61), [werf@fdeabf022](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/fdeabf02227f), [werf#7695](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7695), [werf@666afe129](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/666afe129b11)

#### The Buildah backend is upgraded to upstream Buildah 1.44

<a id="buildah-upgraded-upstream-1-44"></a>`buildah-upgraded-upstream-1-44` · change · `buildah` `dependencies` · products: werf

Before: the Buildah backend (`WERF_BUILDAH_MODE`, `native-rootless`/`native-chroot`) was built from werf's fork of Buildah 1.35 with `containers/common` 0.58, `containers/image` 5.30 and `containers/storage` 1.53.
Now: werf uses upstream Buildah 1.44.1 with `go.podman.io/common` 0.68, `go.podman.io/image` 5.40 and `go.podman.io/storage` 1.63, so Dockerfile builds on the Buildah backend get the Dockerfile features and fixes of these releases. Buildah stays below 1.45 on purpose: with `common` 0.69 rootless builds fail on hosts whose `pasta` is older than 2024-08-14 (e.g. Ubuntu 24.04).
Network-related requirements of the new stack (`netavark`, `pasta`) are described in their own entry.

**References:** [werf@bc51d7214](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/bc51d7214f8e), [werf@fcf48b426](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/fcf48b426014), [werf@6faf9c922](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/6faf9c9224d1)

#### `werf synchronization` accepts the full set of Kubernetes connection flags; its legacy storage flags are documented as ignored

<a id="synchronization-command-flags"></a>`synchronization-command-flags` · change · `locking` `cli` · products: werf

The synchronization subsystem (`--synchronization`/`-S`, `WERF_SYNCHRONIZATION`, the `werf synchronization` server) works as in v2.
Before: `werf synchronization` accepted only `--kube-config`, `--kube-config-base64` and `--kube-context` for connecting to Kubernetes; `--local`, `--local-lock-manager-base-dir`, `--local-stages-storage-cache-base-dir`, `--kubernetes-namespace-prefix` and `--ttl` were described as configuring storage although they had no effect.
Now: `werf synchronization` accepts the same Kubernetes connection flags as other commands (`--kube-api-server`, `--kube-token`, `--kube-token-path`, `--kube-auth-*`, `--kube-context-cluster`, `--kube-context-user`, `--kube-impersonate-*`, `--kube-proxy-url`, `--kube-burst-limit` and their `WERF_*` variables). The five legacy flags are still accepted and are documented as compatibility flags that are ignored: without `--kubernetes`, locks are kept in process memory; with it, they are stored in ConfigMaps of the `werf-synchronization` namespace. When `--synchronization` is set explicitly, werf prints the synchronization server it uses.

**References:** [werf#7603](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7603), [werf#7989](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7989)

### Deploy

#### Chart rendering parses each rendered manifest once

<a id="render-performance-single-manifest-parse"></a>`render-performance-single-manifest-parse` · change · `render` `performance` · products: nelm, werf

Before: every rendered manifest was parsed twice, once only to check it.
Now: each manifest is parsed once, which roughly halves the time and allocations of turning rendered templates into resources; the second parse runs only after decoding fails, so error messages for invalid YAML are unchanged. A few YAML inputs that only the discarded check rejected no longer fail rendering: a tab inside a quoted scalar or a plain scalar starting with `@` now render correctly, while for a `...` document-end marker in the middle of a file the rest of the file is dropped, and a YAML-tagged value becomes empty, without an error. Charts that rendered before render the same. Lint (`nelm chart lint`, `werf lint`) still rejects most of these inputs through resource validation; render does not.

**References:** [nelm#730](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/730)

#### Deploy commands that build no images run without Docker or Buildah

<a id="deploy-chart-only-without-container-backend"></a>`deploy-chart-only-without-container-backend` · change · `cli` `images` · products: werf

Before: `werf converge`, `werf render`, `werf plan`, `werf lint`, `werf helm get-autogenerated-values` and `werf bundle publish` initialized the container backend (Docker or Buildah) on start, so they failed on a host without a working backend even for a project without images.
Now: `werf converge` and `werf render` initialize the backend only when an image actually has to be built. `werf plan`, `werf lint`, `werf helm get-autogenerated-values` and `werf bundle publish` skip it for projects without images and with `--without-images`; `werf plan`, `werf lint` and `werf helm get-autogenerated-values` also with `--stub-tags` or a local repository address, and `werf plan --show-plan` never needs it. Automatic host cleanup runs only if a backend was initialized.

**References:** [werf#7625](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7625), [werf@f447c2c7c](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/f447c2c7c838)

#### Release history is read from storage metadata and release bodies are streamed, cutting memory use

<a id="release-storage-metadata-reads"></a>`release-storage-metadata-reads` · change · `release-storage` `performance` · products: nelm, werf

Before: every action that read release history (`chart render`, `chart lint`, `release plan install`, `release install`, `release rollback`, `release uninstall`, `release list`) fetched and decoded the full body of every stored revision, so time and memory grew with the number and size of revisions; `release list` could run out of memory on clusters with thousands of releases.
Now: revisions are listed from the labels and annotations of the storage objects (Secret, ConfigMap, SQL row) and a revision body is fetched only where the action needs it: `chart render` reads none, `chart lint`, `release plan install`, `release install` and `release uninstall` read the latest one, `release rollback` reads the latest and the target one. `release list` and `release history` stream bodies page by page, keeping only the fields they print; `release list` in table format reads no bodies, and `release history --revisions-limit N` reads only the newest N bodies. The storage format stays Helm-compatible; new revisions additionally carry a `werf.io/release-version: v1` annotation on the storage object, so that release annotations can be read without the body.
Related behavior changes:
- A revision whose body can't be decoded is shown by `release list` and `release history` with its name, namespace, revision and status and `null` details, with an error log, instead of being skipped or replaced by an older revision; history pruning (`--release-history-limit`) now counts and removes such revisions.
- A storage object whose name doesn't match the revision named in its labels, such as a copy of a release Secret, is no longer taken for that revision by listing or pruning.

**References:** [werf#8061](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8061), [werf#8084](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8084), [nelm#723](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/723), [nelm#745](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/745), [nelm#752](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/752)

## Fixes

### General

#### Configuration errors name the config file actually used

<a id="build-errors-name-config-file"></a>`build-errors-name-config-file` · fix · `config` `cli` · products: werf

Before: with `--config another.werf.yaml`, errors said `no image matches pattern "x"`, `... is not defined in werf.yaml`, or `unable to load werf config: ...` without naming the file.
Now: such errors name the config file in use, for example `no image matches pattern "x" in another.werf.yaml`.

**References:** [werf#8154](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8154)

#### Parallel log output no longer races on indentation

<a id="logging-concurrent-indentation-race"></a>`logging-concurrent-indentation-race` · fix · `logging` · products: werf

Before: when several workers logged in parallel (e.g. parallel image builds), one of them temporarily resetting the indentation could affect the indentation of output being formatted concurrently by the others, producing misindented lines.
Now: indentation is updated atomically, so concurrent output keeps its own indentation.

**References:** [werf#7802](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7802), [logboek#81](https://github.com/werf/logboek/pull/81)

#### werf kubectl uses `--kube-config-base64` even when `KUBECONFIG` is set

<a id="kubectl-kube-config-base64-priority"></a>`kubectl-kube-config-base64-priority` · fix · `kubectl` · products: werf

Before: `werf kubectl` ignored `--kube-config-base64` (`$WERF_KUBE_CONFIG_BASE64`) whenever `$WERF_KUBE_CONFIG`, `$WERF_KUBECONFIG` or `$KUBECONFIG` was set, and used that kubeconfig file instead.
Now: `--kube-config-base64` takes priority over the kubeconfig environment variables.

**References:** [werf#7552](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7552)

#### werf no longer crashes when a host lock is acquired exactly at its timeout

<a id="file-lock-timeout-deadlock"></a>`file-lock-timeout-deadlock` · fix · `locking` · products: werf

Before: when a host file lock (e.g. a stage or Git cache lock) was acquired at the very moment its wait timeout expired, werf could crash with `fatal error: all goroutines are asleep - deadlock!`, and a lock acquired at that moment could stay held until the process exited.
Now: the timeout is reported as an error, and a lock acquired at that moment is released.

**References:** [werf#8110](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8110), [lockgate@1a37f08b6](https://github.com/werf/lockgate/commit/1a37f08b6184)

### Build

#### A failed manifest upload is reported instead of being treated as published

<a id="build-registry-upload-eof-errors"></a>`build-registry-upload-eof-errors` · fix · `registry` · products: werf

Before: an image or index manifest upload that ended with EOF could be reported as successful, so later operations failed on a tag that was never published; a failed stage lookup lost the registry's error.
Now: the upload fails with an error, and missing-stage errors include the image reference and the original registry error.

**References:** [werf#8047](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8047)

#### Buildah builds no longer leave working containers behind

<a id="build-buildah-leaked-containers"></a>`build-buildah-leaked-containers` · fix · `buildah` `dockerfile` · products: werf

Before: with the Buildah backend, a staged Dockerfile build (`staged: true`) with `COPY --from` left a temporary source container mounted for every copy, and a Dockerfile build that failed midway left its `<image-id>-working-container`; these containers piled up in the containers storage and pinned their images.
Now: temporary and working containers are removed after the copy and after a failed build.

**References:** [werf#7938](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7938)

#### Changing only the mode or the path of a Git file (for example, the executable bit or a rename) triggers a rebuild

<a id="build-git-file-mode-in-checksum"></a>`build-git-file-mode-in-checksum` · fix · `git` `cache` · products: werf

Before: checksums of Git files used for `git.stageDependencies` and for the build context of Dockerfile images took only file contents into account, so a mode-only change such as `chmod +x`, or renaming a file without changing its contents, did not rerun dependent stages or rebuild the image.
Now: the file mode and the file path are part of the checksum, and such changes are detected.

**References:** [werf@15e7ca21d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/15e7ca21d13f), [werf#7940](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7940)

#### Dockerfile images are rebuilt when a file used by `RUN --mount=type=bind` changes

<a id="build-dockerfile-run-bind-mount-digest"></a>`build-dockerfile-run-bind-mount-digest` · fix · `dockerfile` `cache` · products: werf

Before: for Dockerfile images built without `staged: true`, the stage digest included `RUN` instruction text and checksums only of `COPY`/`ADD` sources, so changing a build-context file read through `RUN --mount=type=bind,source=...` reused the cached image while `docker build` would rerun the instruction.
Now: sources of context bind mounts (without `from=`) are checksummed, with `ARG`/`ENV` values expanded; an unresolved source tracks the whole context. Digests of Dockerfiles without context bind mounts are unchanged; images using such mounts are rebuilt once.

**References:** [werf#8080](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8080), [werf#8115](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8115), <https://github.com/werf/werf/issues/6823>

#### Files with special characters in their names that are deleted in Git are removed from Stapel images

<a id="build-git-deleted-quoted-paths"></a>`build-git-deleted-quoted-paths` · fix · `git` `stapel` · products: werf

Before: when a file whose path Git quotes in diffs (non-ASCII characters, spaces at the end, quotes, control characters) was deleted between commits, the Stapel git patch did not remove it from the image: werf parsed the quoted path literally.
Now: quoted paths of deleted files are unquoted, and such files are removed from the image like any other deleted file.

**References:** [werf#8171](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8171)

#### Git mapping `owner` and `group` are applied consistently to all added files and directories

<a id="build-stapel-git-mapping-ownership"></a>`build-stapel-git-mapping-ownership` · fix · `stapel` `git` · products: werf

Before: with the Docker backend, two git mappings of the same content with different `owner`/`group` shared one Git archive, so files could get the ownership of whichever mapping created the archive first. In incremental builds (Git patches) on both Docker and Buildah, directories that first appeared in a patch were owned by `root:root` instead of the mapping's `owner`/`group`, unlike a from-scratch build of the same commit.
Now: the mapping's `owner`/`group` (root when omitted) is applied to every extracted file, directory and symlink, including directories created by patches. Already built images are not repaired automatically; rebuild them if needed.

**References:** [werf#7972](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7972), [werf#7977](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7977)

#### Native Buildah Dockerfile builds no longer share secrets and SSH settings with other builds

<a id="build-buildah-isolated-build-options"></a>`build-buildah-isolated-build-options` · fix · `buildah` `dockerfile` · products: werf

Before: with the native Buildah backend (`WERF_BUILDAH_MODE=native-chroot` or `native-rootless`), a Dockerfile build wrote its `secrets` and `ssh` settings into build options shared by the whole werf process, so a later Dockerfile image without `secrets` built in the same run got the secrets of a previous one, and images built in parallel overwrote each other's secrets and SSH sources.
Now: every Dockerfile build and every Stapel container gets its own copy of the options, so `secrets` and `ssh` apply only to the image that configures them.

**References:** [werf#7798](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7798)

#### Native Buildah builds look up local images faster on hosts with many images

<a id="build-buildah-faster-local-image-lookups"></a>`build-buildah-faster-local-image-lookups` · fix · `buildah` `performance` · products: werf

Before: on hosts with a populated local image store, the native Buildah backend resolved image references repeatedly for every inventory candidate, slowing builds down.
Now: the inspected image ID is used directly, and project stage images are selected with an exact `<project>:*` filter.

**References:** [werf#8064](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8064)

#### Parallel build logs no longer show `�` in place of multi-byte characters

<a id="logging-parallel-build-utf8-mojibake"></a>`logging-parallel-build-utf8-mojibake` · fix · `logging` · products: werf

Before: during parallel image builds, a multi-byte UTF-8 character (for example, the `└`, `┌`, `│` log tree prefixes) that straddled a 1024-byte chunk of a worker's buffered output was split and printed as `�`.
Now: incomplete UTF-8 sequences are held back until complete, including when a worker finishes writing, so the output is not corrupted.

**References:** [werf#7632](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7632), [werf@eda346e7f](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/eda346e7f948)

#### Registry tokens are refreshed correctly for registries that redirect to another host

<a id="build-registry-token-cache-redirects"></a>`build-registry-token-cache-redirects` · fix · `registry` · products: werf

Before: the registry bearer-token cache could keep reusing a token that a redirected host (GHCR, Quay, ACR and similar redirect blob requests to storage hosts) had rejected, because the rejection could not invalidate the cache entry of the origin registry; the cache also stopped reusing tokens for such registries altogether, and deleting tags from a GitLab registry exchanged a new token for every tag.
Now: tokens whose scope was named by a redirected host's bearer challenge are exchanged afresh, tokens for the registry's own scopes keep being served from the cache, and GitLab tag deletion reuses one token per scope.

**References:** [werf@a84a30b1f](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/a84a30b1f2d1), [werf#7979](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7979)

#### Staged Dockerfile builds honor `COPY --parents` and `COPY`/`ADD --exclude`

<a id="build-staged-dockerfile-copy-parents-exclude"></a>`build-staged-dockerfile-copy-parents-exclude` · fix · `dockerfile` `buildah` · products: werf

Before: in Dockerfile images with `staged: true` (Buildah backend), `COPY --parents` was silently ignored and sources were flattened into the destination, and `COPY --exclude`/`ADD --exclude` were ignored, so excluded files ended up in the image.
Now: `--parents` preserves the source directory structure under the destination (also for a single file source, for example `COPY --parents ./src/./bin/app /dst` creates `/dst/bin/app`), and `--exclude` patterns are applied. Non-staged builds already behaved this way.

**References:** [werf#7690](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7690), [werf#7691](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7691), [werf#7693](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7693)

#### `COPY` and `ADD` heredocs work in Dockerfile images with `staged: true`

<a id="build-staged-dockerfile-copy-heredocs"></a>`build-staged-dockerfile-copy-heredocs` · fix · `dockerfile` · products: werf

Before: with `staged: true`, `COPY <<EOF /dst` failed with `heredoc is not supported with COPY command`, and forms such as `COPY --chmod=755 <<EOF /dst` or `COPY <<A <<B /dst/` failed with `unable to calculate build context globs checksum`.
Now: such Dockerfiles build and produce the same files as `docker build`.

**References:** [werf#8155](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8155), <https://github.com/werf/werf/issues/6521>

#### `werf export --use-build-report` exports images published to the final repository

<a id="build-export-use-build-report-final-repo"></a>`build-export-use-build-report-final-repo` · fix · `images` `build-report` · products: werf

Before: with `--final-repo` (in particular together with `--repo :local`), `werf export --use-build-report` looked up the reported final images in the primary storage and could fail to export them; with the Buildah backend, the ID of an inspected OCI image could be empty.
Now: when a build-report record points to the final repository, the image is exported from there, and the Buildah backend takes the image ID from the container storage.

**References:** [werf@870a276de](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/870a276de590)

### Deploy

#### A release with an internal `state=ready` deploy dependency is skipped when nothing changed

<a id="deploy-skip-unchanged-with-ready-dependency"></a>`deploy-skip-unchanged-with-ready-dependency` · fix · `plan` `tracking` `annotations` · products: nelm, werf

Before: a chart with a resource having an internal `werf.io/deploy-dependency-<id>: state=ready,...` on a resource of the same stage was never considered up to date: every redeploy without changes created a new revision and ran hooks, because the dependency target was always forced into readiness tracking.
Now: readiness tracking of the target is forced only when a resource that depends on it is created, updated, recreated, applied or tracked in the same deploy, so an unchanged release is skipped. A changed target whose dependents are all unchanged is tracked according to its own annotations (`werf.io/fail-mode`, `werf.io/track-termination-mode`) instead of always failing the whole deploy immediately.

**References:** [werf#8123](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8123), [nelm#789](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/789)

#### A release with unchanged numeric `--set` values is skipped as up to date

<a id="deploy-numeric-set-values-up-to-date"></a>`deploy-numeric-set-values-up-to-date` · fix · `values` `plan` · products: nelm, werf

Before: with a number passed by `--set` (e.g. `--set replicas=3`), every `release install` created a new revision and reran hooks, and `release plan install` reported that the release values changed, because the number from `--set` and the same number read back from the stored release were compared as different types.
Now: values are compared by their JSON representation, so an unchanged release is skipped (`Skipped release ...: cluster resources already as desired`) and the plan shows no changes. Real changes, including a number replaced with a string, still create a new revision. Templates still see `--set` numbers as integers.

**References:** [werf#8128](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8128), [nelm#786](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/786)

#### Deploy and delete dependency annotations wait for every matching resource

<a id="dependency-annotations-match-all-resources"></a>`dependency-annotations-match-all-resources` · fix · `annotations` `plan` · products: nelm, werf

Before: when a `werf.io/deploy-dependency-<id>` or `werf.io/delete-dependency-<id>` annotation matched several resources of the release (e.g. no `name` given), the annotated resource waited for only one of them, picked arbitrarily.
Now: it waits for all matching resources to be present, ready or absent, as the annotation requires.

**References:** [nelm@3ef6dc9bd](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/3ef6dc9bdf4b)

#### Deploy doesn't wait for PVCs and PVs removed from the chart to disappear

<a id="deploy-removed-pvc-no-absence-wait"></a>`deploy-removed-pvc-no-absence-wait` · fix · `resources` `tracking` · products: nelm, werf

Before: a PersistentVolumeClaim or PersistentVolume removed from the chart was deleted before the release resources were deployed, and the deploy waited for it to disappear. A PVC stays `Terminating` while old Pods use it (a PV while it is bound), and those Pods are replaced only later in the same deploy, so the deploy hung until the timeout.
Now: on install, upgrade and rollback, removed PVCs and PVs are deleted without waiting for their absence. Explicit dependencies on their absence still wait for them, and `release uninstall` still waits.

**References:** [nelm#777](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/777)

#### Deployment tracking fails fast when the new ReplicaSet cannot create pods

<a id="tracking-deployment-pod-create-failures"></a>`tracking-deployment-pod-create-failures` · fix · `tracking` · products: nelm, werf

Before: when the new ReplicaSet of a Deployment could not create pods (the `ReplicaFailure` condition with reason `FailedCreate`, e.g. `exceeded quota`, an invalid pod spec, or a webhook rejection), tracking only saw transient Warning events, missed failures that happened before tracking started, and usually waited until the tracking timeout.
Now: the `ReplicaFailure` condition of the Deployment's own new ReplicaSet is read directly.
- An invalid pod spec, or a quota shortage that the rollout cannot release by scaling old pods down (confirmed against the pod list and the `ResourceQuota` and held for about 10 seconds), fails the resource immediately, regardless of `werf.io/failures-allowed-per-replica`; with `werf.io/fail-mode: IgnoreAndContinueDeployProcess` the deploy still continues.
- Other pod-create failures, including quota shortages that the rollout can recover from, are counted against `werf.io/failures-allowed-per-replica`, each failure once (previously an event-sourced Deployment failure was counted again on every later status update).
- Confirming a quota deadlock needs `list pods` and `get resourcequotas` in the namespace; without these permissions such failures stay counted.

**References:** [nelm#780](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/780), [kubedog@10db28fc1](https://github.com/werf/kubedog/commit/10db28fc11a0), [kubedog@38643e953](https://github.com/werf/kubedog/commit/38643e953de5), [kubedog@8ceef4c3c](https://github.com/werf/kubedog/commit/8ceef4c3c442), [kubedog@8bcce864f](https://github.com/werf/kubedog/commit/8bcce864f0ad), <https://github.com/werf/kubedog/issues/398>

#### Resources removed from the chart are deleted after a pending or failed revision

<a id="deploy-delete-resources-after-pending-revision"></a>`deploy-delete-resources-after-pending-revision` · fix · `resources` `plan` `uninstall` · products: nelm, werf

Before: deletions were computed only against the last revision. If that revision hung (`pending-upgrade`) or failed before its deletions ran, resources that were in the last deployed revision and were removed from the chart stayed in the cluster forever; `release uninstall` had the same gap and then removed the release history.
Now: `release install`, `release plan install`, `release rollback`, remote `chart lint` and `release uninstall` (werf: `converge`, `plan`, `rollback`, `dismiss`, `bundle apply`, `bundle plan`) also delete the resources that only the last deployed revision has. They are only deleted, never validated or installed, and their hooks don't run. Resources adopted by another release, with `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep` or with `werf.io/ownership: anyone` are still not deleted. On the first deploy after such a revision the plan may show extra `delete` operations. Resources left over by earlier deploys whose following revision is already deployed are not cleaned up.

**References:** [werf#8125](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8125), [nelm#792](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/792)

#### Revisions left pending by an interrupted deploy are marked `failed` by the next successful deploy

<a id="release-pending-revisions-marked-failed"></a>`release-pending-revisions-marked-failed` · fix · `release-storage` · products: nelm, werf

Before: if a deploy was interrupted (CI timeout, `kill`) while its revision was `pending-install`, `pending-upgrade` or `pending-rollback`, the revision stayed pending forever, and `release history` (`helm history`) showed an operation in progress that didn't exist.
Now: a successful install, upgrade, rollback or auto-rollback marks every earlier `pending-*` revision `failed` at the end of the deploy, keeping its deployment timestamps. A failed deploy doesn't change them. A pending revision whose body can't be read is skipped with a warning.

**References:** [werf#8131](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8131), [nelm#798](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/798)

#### Rollback expands Lists and converts Secret `stringData` like install

<a id="release-rollback-normalized-stored-manifests"></a>`release-rollback-normalized-stored-manifests` · fix · `rollback` `resources` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `nelm release rollback` and `werf rollback` deployed and stored the manifests of the target revision as they were. For a revision stored without Nelm's normalization (for example by Helm), `kind: List` manifests were not expanded into their items and Secret `stringData` was not converted to `data`, unlike `nelm release install`.
Now: rollback expands Lists and converts Secret `stringData` to base64 `data` before storing the new revision and deploying it, like install. The manifests stored in the rollback revision can therefore differ in form from those of the target revision.

**References:** [nelm#624](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/624)

#### Stopping progress output right after it starts no longer races

<a id="tracking-progress-printer-start-stop-race"></a>`tracking-progress-printer-start-stop-race` · fix · `tracking` `logging` · products: nelm, werf

Before: the periodic progress tables printed during deploy, rollback and uninstall were initialized inside a background goroutine, so stopping or waiting for them immediately after start (e.g. a very short uninstall) could read uninitialized state, which could crash or hang the command.
Now: the printer is fully initialized before its background goroutine starts, so it can be stopped at any time.

**References:** [werf#7805](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7805), [nelm#690](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/690)

#### Values and dependency messages of the embedded Helm go through the Nelm logger and `--log-level`

<a id="logging-helm-fork-messages-nelm-logger"></a>`logging-helm-fork-messages-nelm-logger` · fix · `logging` `values` · products: nelm, werf

Before: values coalescing warnings (e.g. `cannot overwrite table with non table for ...`) and the `requirements.yaml` deprecation warnings of the embedded Helm were printed only at `--log-level` `debug`/`trace` and to stdout, where they got mixed into `chart render` manifests.
Now: these messages go through the Nelm logger: warnings are shown on stderr at `warning` and `info` levels (hidden at `error`/`silent`, which includes the default level of `chart render`); Helm debug messages are shown at `debug`/`trace`. The values type mismatch error names the full path and types, e.g. `type mismatch on p.mid.leaf: expected a table, got string (some-string)` instead of `type mismatch on leaf: %!t(string=some-string)`, and dependency processing errors name the subchart.

**References:** [werf#8136](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8136), [nelm#805](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/805)

#### `--no-pod-logs` applies when installing from a saved plan and to tracking of dependencies

<a id="plan-use-plan-no-pod-logs"></a>`plan-use-plan-no-pod-logs` · fix · `plan` `tracking` `logging` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `release plan install` didn't apply `--no-pod-logs` to the plan it saved, so `nelm release install --use-plan` (werf: `werf converge --use-plan`) always showed pod logs; readiness tracking for deploy dependencies ignored the flag too.
Now: `--no-pod-logs` is applied whenever a plan is executed, in addition to the `werf.io/skip-logs` annotation.

**References:** [werf#8092](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8092), [nelm@30650512b](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/30650512b08a)

#### `WERF_NO_POD_LOGS` disables Pod logs

<a id="tracking-werf-no-pod-logs-env"></a>`tracking-werf-no-pod-logs-env` · fix · `tracking` `logging` · products: werf

Before: the help of `--no-pod-logs` in `werf converge`, `werf bundle apply`, `werf rollback` and other tracking commands named `$WERF_NO_POD_LOGS` as its default, but the variable was never read: only the flag disabled Pod logs.
Now: `WERF_NO_POD_LOGS=true` disables collecting and printing Pod logs, like `--no-pod-logs`.

**References:** [werf#8091](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8091)

#### `export-values` no longer depend on the order of dependencies in `Chart.yaml`

<a id="values-export-values-dependency-order"></a>`values-export-values-dependency-order` · fix · `values` `dependencies` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `export-values` from the charts' `values.yaml` and `secret-values.yaml` read each dependency's parent values once, in `Chart.yaml` order, so an export whose `parent:` path was written by an export to a sibling dependency listed later got the sibling's default value.
Now: exports are ordered so that an export waits for the exports that write to its `parent:` path, also in nested charts, whichever order the dependencies are listed in. When two exports write the same child path, the one declared later still wins. Ordering many exports is fast (topological sort).

**References:** [werf#8134](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8134), [werf#8138](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8138), [nelm#804](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/804), [nelm#807](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/807)

#### `export-values` of `global.*` declared in a nested chart read the root chart's globals

<a id="values-export-values-nested-global"></a>`values-export-values-nested-global` · fix · `values` `dependencies` · products: nelm, werf

Before: an `export-values` entry with `parent: global.X` declared in an intermediate chart (root → mid → leaf, the export in `mid/Chart.yaml`) read only mid's own `global`, so `--set global.X=...`, `global` in the root `values.yaml` and service values such as `global.werf.images.*` were ignored, and mid's `values.yaml` `global` won over `--set global...`.
Now: such exports read the root chart's `global` merged over the globals of the charts in between, the same way Helm propagates globals to subcharts: the higher chart wins, maps are merged, and between values layers the higher layer still wins.

**References:** [werf#8130](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8130), [nelm#794](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/794)

#### `secret-values.yaml` of subcharts not listed in `dependencies` is applied

<a id="secrets-subchart-secret-values-undeclared"></a>`secrets-subchart-secret-values-undeclared` · fix · `secrets` `values` `dependencies` · products: nelm, werf

Before: the `secret-values.yaml` of a subchart in `charts/` that the parent doesn't declare in `Chart.yaml` `dependencies` was silently ignored when rendering it as a subchart (it was applied only as a side effect of `export-values` processing of declared dependencies).
Now: every subchart gets its `secret-values.yaml` merged over its `values.yaml`, declared or not, at the same level: subchart `values.yaml` < subchart `secret-values.yaml` < the parent's values for the subchart. `--no-default-secret-values` ignores the `secret-values.yaml` of the subcharts too. Dependency conditions and tags still don't see subchart secret values.

**References:** [werf#8129](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8129), [nelm#795](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/795)

#### werf plan no longer leaves the `--secret-key` value in the werf process environment

<a id="secrets-werf-secret-key-not-left-in-env"></a>`secrets-werf-secret-key-not-left-in-env` · fix · `secrets` · products: werf

Before: after the plan step of `werf plan` and `werf bundle plan`, a key passed with `--secret-key` stayed set as `WERF_SECRET_KEY` in the werf process, so everything started later by the same process (child processes such as kubeconfig exec plugins, later deploy steps without an explicit key) inherited it instead of using `.werf_secret_key` or `~/.werf/global_secret_key`.
Now: the key is set only while the Nelm action runs, and the previous value of `WERF_SECRET_KEY` (or its absence) is restored afterwards.

**References:** [werf#8126](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8126)

### Cleanup

#### Automatic host cleanup honors custom `--home-dir` and `--tmp-dir`

<a id="host-cleanup-auto-custom-home-tmp-dir"></a>`host-cleanup-auto-custom-home-tmp-dir` · fix · `host-cleanup` · products: werf

Before: with `--home-dir`/`--tmp-dir` set on the command line, werf started the background automatic host cleanup with `WERF_HOME`/`WERF_TMP_DIR` set to a Go pointer value (e.g. `0xc000123456`) instead of the path, so the cleanup worked on the wrong directories and the custom ones were not cleaned automatically.
Now: the actual paths are passed to the background cleanup.

**References:** [werf@81cf86ff6](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/81cf86ff6a2d)

#### Listing local project stages is much faster on hosts with many images

<a id="host-cleanup-faster-local-stage-listing"></a>`host-cleanup-faster-local-stage-listing` · fix · `host-cleanup` `performance` · products: werf

Before: listing a project's stages in local storage (used when werf works without `--repo`, e.g. `werf purge`, project-scoped host purge, `werf stages copy` from local storage) asked Docker to filter images by both repository reference and the `werf` label, which took seconds per request on hosts with many images.
Now: Docker filters by reference only and werf checks the `werf` label itself, with the same result much faster.

**References:** [werf#7907](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7907)

#### `werf cleanup --dry-run` no longer records a cleanup run in the repository

<a id="cleanup-dry-run-no-registry-writes"></a>`cleanup-dry-run-no-registry-writes` · fix · `cleanup` · products: werf

Before: `werf cleanup --dry-run` without a separate `--meta-repo` still pushed the last-cleanup record to the repository, so a dry run counted as a cleanup and suppressed the warning that cleanup is overdue.
Now: a dry run only calculates and reports what would be deleted and does not write anything to the repository.

**References:** [werf#7960](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7960)

#### `werf cleanup` no longer deletes final images published by a concurrent build

<a id="cleanup-concurrent-final-images-race"></a>`cleanup-concurrent-final-images-race` · fix · `cleanup` · products: werf

Before: with `--final-repo`, `werf cleanup` running concurrently with a build could read the primary repository before the build published a stage and the final repository after it published the final copy, treat the new final image as an orphan and delete it.
Now: cleanup lists the final repository before the managed images, metadata and primary repository, so images published during cleanup are not deleted as orphans.

**References:** [werf#7975](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7975)

#### `werf host purge` removes all Stapel containers and volumes it can and reports every failure

<a id="host-purge-stapel-continue-on-errors"></a>`host-purge-stapel-continue-on-errors` · fix · `host-cleanup` `stapel` · products: werf

Before: `werf host purge` stopped at the first Docker error while removing Stapel containers, e.g. a container still used by a concurrent build: the remaining Stapel containers, their volumes and the stapel image stayed on the host, and only that first error was reported.
Now: `werf host purge` removes every Stapel container and volume werf owns even if removing another one fails, keeps a container whose volume is still mounted by another container, then tries to remove the stapel image (which fails while a container of that version is left), and reports all failures together.

**References:** [werf#7978](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7978)
